Spec Ops: The Line is a game where everything but the gameplay is top notch. What it does well is the setting which is the beautiful Dubai and the time they put into the detail made me really believe I was there. I especially liked the fish tanks. The amazing soundtrack which features Deep Purple and Jimi Hendrix and the absolutely excellent voice acting surpised me and there was a great plot with a tweeeest.

It's just a shame that despite all this, the gameplay is just bog standard third person shooting you've seen in a million and one games already. It's all go into next room, suspiciously also full of chest high objects to take cover behind (!) and kill them nasty americans before moving on which has been done to death. There are some neat little things they've added though such as shooting windows with sand behind will crush the enemies dumb enough to stand next to them.

Moving on, there are some powerful scenes in this game. My personal favourite is the [spoiler]white phosporus[/spoiler] scene, it just hits you hard once you've realised what you've done. It's clear the game wants to think about what you're being ordered to do and in the finale basically tells you that you're far from the hero you think you are. It's a rather hamfisted way to get you to think about what you're doing in other games but I admire the devs for doing this.

The voice acting changes throughout the game, as the missions and the plot progresses you and your men go from calmly talking and ordering around to full on shouting. I really like this as it does help the plot convey how far gone the main character is. Another part of the audio is the soundtrack, it matches the tone of every situation you're in and the radio man really knows how to set the mood when he deploys songs like [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2-uuvGm31bk]Nowhere to Run[/url]. 

In conclusion, Spec Ops: The Line is a great game to pick up. It's an enjoyable experience which could've been amazing if not for the typical whack-a-mole third person gameplay. Pick it up for £10 or less if you can.

[h1][b]Spec Ops: The Line is influenced by the novella "Heart of Darkness" and by the movie "Apocalypse Now"[/b] [/h1]

[h1][i]The Line is an emotional rollercoaster that makes you question your actions and motives.[/i][/h1]

[b][u]The Gameplay:[/u][/b]
Spec Ops: The Line is your typical cover based TPS (Third-Person Shooter). It features your average modern weapons that you can see in other shooters that take place in a modern day setting: Call of Duty, Battlefield etc.
There is also the two gun limit like in many other modern shooters: Primary weapon / Secondary weapon.

The gameplay itself is not innovative at all. It doesn't add anything new to the genre: Shoot, take cover, shoot, run to the next cover, shoot - repeat
You can assign different tasks to your two squadmates but you don't need to use them THAT much...or you barely use 'em at all. The tasks themselves are quite basic: "Mark and attack that target" "Shoot that thingy over there" etc.

I have to say, though, that the gameplay in The Line is very smooth and the cover mechanics are one of the best i've seen. Sprinting to cover and vaulting over cover is very smooth. The gameplay is good, fast and smooth...very well done. It's just that it doesn't add anything new. 

[b][u]The Story[/u][/b]
Spec Ops: The Line may seem like your average military shooter at first but make no mistake! It is quite the opposite.
The game doesn't glorify war. You may play the game for 30-40 minutes and think that it's another one of these "murika fu'k yeh" games but it's not. 
The story will change soon and it keeps coming up with surprises till the very end of the game. I can't say much about the story without giving away spoilers but all you need to know is this: [b]This game has a story that has NEVER been done before in the TPS/FPS genre. When it comes to video gaming then this story is an unique pearl.[/b]
You have to trust me on this one.

I wanted to revisit this review, as I've thought much on the overly praised games that have "defined" video game story telling, despite working entirely against the very nature of story telling in video games.

Video games are narratives of choice - whether it's an actual RPG with dialogue options or COD, you choose what you say or when you pull the trigger. Storytelling in the video game medium is best expressed when you are given as much freedom of choice as possible, and the writers/developers take into account different ways the story flows. You can do this with an extremely meticulous hand, curating different content for different actions and choices (say in an RPG like Knights of the Old Republic 2); or you can grant as much lightweight leeway as possible, providing the same basic structured experience but allowing the player to drive how everything occurs (think something like Dark Souls, where half the experience is what you are able to find and what order you find it in, painting the revealing a different narrative through the partial puzzle you uniquely experience).

Now take Spec Ops - it does neither of these things. It is an attempted moral judgement of a character, and the attempted meta judgement of the player. It places war crimes in the path of bland shooting mechanics, and tells us how terrible we (the character, and the player) are for our actions. Why don't we just turn around, and leave Dubai? Why are we doing this?

The answer is because they make you do it, if you play the game. There is no choice presented in this narrative - the game accounts for no deviations from its narrow clone of Heart of Darkness. When you see the horror you have inflicted, how can it have any impact if you had no choice BUT to commit the horror?

Basically this is not a game, it is a film that doesn't like games. It lacks game story-telling, and  its gameplay mechanics (shooting, movement, etc) are garbage. This game pretends to be terrible in the course of its narrative. Turns out, we are what we pretend to be.

I chose not to be chided. I uninstalled the game. The narrative could have been good, if the choice had actually existed.

Spec Ops is a strange, yet very interesting beast.

It starts off like one of theses bombastic console shooters (Call of Duty, Gears of Wars 2, ...) both in terms of gameplay (lots of cutscenes and action set pieces), and story (Americans going at the opposite side of the world to kill baddies). But after the first mission, which is also the tutorial, it suddenly takes a more interesting turn.

On the gameplay side, the game is a third person, cover-based, shooter but is more interesting than others cover based titles. A rudimentary command system allows you to give some orders to your AI teammates. The level design is also well done, with more verticality than most shooters. Combining the command system with a clever use of the map allow for nice flanking positions. That feels very satisfying when you can dispatch a wave of ennemies by being actually clever rather than just rushing in. It's also a lot more dynamic and interesting than the extremely static "first guy to raise his head above his barricade is dead" gameplay of Gears of War 2.

On the story side, well...it's hard to talk about it without spoiling, but i will just say that it will soon take an unexpected turn. That story is interesting enough that i enjoyed playing the game twice (something i usually never do, even when i like a game). It allowed me to find some details that i didn't notice on my first playthrough (such as paintings on the walls, or references in the NPC dialogs) as well as better understand the story and its characters.

The game however is not perfect. 

On the story side, it's not conveyed perfectly. It tries to be interesting with many stuff happening (again, i'm trying to not spoil), but it's sometimes more confusing than it should be due to some slightly wonky dialogs from time to tim (either too heavy-handed, or on the contrary not explaining enough). The second playthrough will of course help clear out any remaining doubt you may have on the story

On the gameplay side, the controls are clearly made for console, and are therefore annoying to use on PC (many buttons have 2 or 3 roles, which lead to confusion and stupid deaths while in battle). I would have wished to be able to rebind all actions separately. Another annoyance is that there are still some of theses set action pieces (such as defending with an infinite ammo turret) that you get in the bombastic shooters. The kind of stuff that are exhilarating the first time you encounter them in a game, but get annoying when all games have them. Finally, and probably the biggest issue, is that it shares some of the usual problems of cover-based shooters. If you're next to a ledge/barricade, but not actually in cover, you magically can't fire down the ledge and you take more damage even though the barricade should protect you. That's annoying, but well, it's part of the genre that you have to stay in cover every single time.

On the whole, Spec Ops feels like a game that has some slight issues, but is original and interesting enough to have its own charm, and i find it quite endearing. It will remain as an interesting experimentation, and i'm sad it didn't have more commercial success, as I'm sure a spiritual sequel would have fixed the small issues while keeping what makes it good. I recommend it if you like solo shooters, but want a deeper story experience than what Call of Duty-style game offer.

One of the most unusual single-player first person shooters that I've played, Spec Ops: The Line takes a page out of Heart of Darkness with a strange and dark descent into THE FEELS. If you like going around slaughtering waves of baddies without remorse  or consequence, this probably isn't the best game for you. Mired in real moral dilemmas where you really don't have any good options; and yet have to live with the consequences, conveys a depth of emotion uncommon for a video game (and First-Person Shooters especially). This game is great at drawing the player in, and showing them the bad side of combat. That having been said... its slightly painful to play. Negative feelings like regret, remorse, fear, helplessness, anger, guilt... are usually the kinds of feelings people try to avoid, or at least take in small doses. This game gets pretty intense and immersive, as the player increasingly feels as the character feels. If I might sum it up in a phrase: Spec Ops: The Line is the best game that I never want to play again. But its definitely worth experiencing once.

Now, a quick breakdown of the game's qualities...
---- THE GOOD ----
* Departure from the standard FPS tropes
* Interesting characters
* Interesting storyline
* Amazing ability to make the player feel unnerved, especially towards the end
* Really great level design
* Great atmosphere
* Love the voice acting

---- THE BAD ----
* Short game. I think I finished it in about 11 hours
* Nothing really innovative with the gameplay. Everything amazing is in the story and setting. Outside of that its mostly a standard FPS
* The Feels can get a bit intense and make the player uncomfortable.
* Graphics seem really dated, even when it first came out. Not quite sure what I dislike about them....
* Controls could be tightened. Tends to feel a bit sluggish in a large firefight, but maybe with a newer PC it would be fine

Thats about it. I give this game a 7.5/10 . That might be lower than it deserves. I did enjoy it, but I wish it were longer and more gradual. I also kinda wanted it to end towards the end 'cuz it was getting very dark and very negative. Then there's the sub-par graphics and sluggishness, and that's what I felt 7.5 was a bit more appropriate.

Hope this review helped, thanks!

Spec Ops: The Line is truly one of the most underrated game, modern millitary shooter EVER, and its sickening in every way imagineable. A more honest and factual game about war, that tells war as a one of the most horrible act that humans have ever done, a game that tells you the reality of war, especially from psychological, morality, and phillospical standpoint is heartbreakingly pretty much unknown.

Spec Ops: The Line, despite its not that impressive name (oh, that "Spec Ops" give me an impression of a cliche'd and poorly made U.S soldier heroism-themed game, could've been better if they just named it "The Line") turns out to be a very emotional, memorable, and fantastic game of 2012, and the last 5 years, probably even for the next coming years. It's a rare game, especially in this oversaturated modern millitary game, that it so AWESOME it doesn't even need a sequel, and I'm not even being sarcastic. 

Story (10/10)

The Line (to shortened it, and because I like the name better) takes you to a story of Captain Walker and his Delta squad in a mission to Dubai to rescue and evacuate survivors and to search Walker's most honored comrade, John Konrad. Seems like just another day of run and gun mililtary game, right? Nope, not at all. It do have the basic premise, it do have a so-so, and even slow start (which actually help up to build the general feeling and atmosphere), but fortunately that slow start really pay off and feel like its necessary for the story progression. And that's all what you need to know.

The story is the ultimate driving force of this game, inspired by "Heart of Darkness", which is I don't read it myself yet (that's my longtime homework), that inspired a movie called "Apocalypse Now", having watched the Redux version of Apocalpse Now (and love it wholeheartedly) I know what to expect from this game, its not your typical modern millitary game, rather than pure soldier heroism, The Line tackle themes like morality of war, PTSD, and the darkest side of both war and human's nature. When morality and humnism collides with duty, obsession, and the will to survive, a man's  rational and sanity can be pushed to the very edge of madness and depression. 

"I thought we're here to rescue people"

The Line is a beautifully horrible experience, its like a surrealistic painting, it looks well...surreal and full of unexplained ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but somehow it has magical spell that make you appreciate the art as something meaningful and beautiful depite its sometimes disturbing look. So does The Line, its surreal, full of twist and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, disturbing, and even disgusting in a point, Yet, its still a brilliant and one of the most beautifully written game that will make you stop and think, about the consequences of war, consequences of every choices you made, and will raise a lot of question and interpretaion as you move along. 

The Line is a game with extreme detail of storytelling, making sure there's no plot holes and illogical plot progression yet it still retain its surrelistic aspect and able to  raise a good amount of question and interpretaion for the players to evaluate and speculate. And the character, both cast and development is OUTSTANDING. They feel so alive, very emotional, much human. Wow. Well, yeah, I mean it. And once again, the subtle things is the greatest aspect of the game, and it applicable to the character.

"I've saved so many lives Captain, but I've killed so much more".

Gameplay (8.7/10)

The weakest part of the game, but still the gameplay is incredibly tight, intense, and solid. It's just that, the control and default key binding is not the most confortable I've experienced so far. There's nothing really innovative or noteworthy about the gameplay, but it does the job very well. The Line is a third person, cover-based millitary game. Oh yea, firstly, the gameplay section, and even sound and graphic section will be filled with the element that could've belong to the Story section, because once again its the ULTIMATE driving force of The Line. 

"There must be another option, THERE IS another option"
" No, there really isn't"

The "choice" system is the most unique and the probably the best I've ever seen in a game. One thing I can say, its war, when you faced by two (or more) chocies, the latter doesn't make the former any better, vice versa. Every action has its consequences, and I must say it again..this is war, the conseuquences are unsatisfactory and bitter, and will always be. Sometimes the choice do matter, sometimes doesn't. Sometimes we have to choose to sacrifice between yourself or the other, sometimes we faced an inevitable chocies, sometimes we don't really have any other choice.

The subtlety and the "smaller, more detailed" things in The Line is the more interesting part of the game, This is surprisngly where The Line shines through. As I said, this game is about extreme detail of storytelling, that affect the other aspect of the game like gameplay, sound and in a way, graphic. As for the gameplay, I can't really tell the "little detail", since I can't seem to word it out, and I might be spoiling something along the way. But, then again, The Line is a simple, action-packed, third person game, with enough intensity to keep you hooked to the game, with enough variety of weapons and enemies, and also a simple yet effective tactical commands.

And for the A.I, they're  competent and smart enough to give me a good deal of challenge, and I must say that I get the "Max Payne 3" feeling, simple, action-packed run and gun with heavy emphasis of storytelling, a bit repetitive but.. (continues to graphic section)

Graphic (9.2 / 10)

...the level design and set pieces is  pretty amazing and well thought of, that it retain a sense of vairety and familliarity in the same time. It is varied, but you won't feel like you're moving to another place that is in another continent, you're still in Dubai from start to finsih, but you won't feel bored. The use of Unreal Engine 3 give me the "Bioshock Infinite" feel (which is another example of great storytelling in a game), no,no, not that UE3 games looks like BioShock Infinite, but its more like the atmosphere, the presentation of the game. While BioShock Infinite is a mixture of cinematic-fantasy, The Line is cinematic-reality. And the use of UE3 is the best choice, I like the rough look of UE3 (Rainbow Six Vegas is one example) gives you a sense of reality and believable atmosphere at the course of the game. The effects is done right, not underused nor overused, giving both realistic and dramatic feel in the same time. The animation is fluid and well done overall. I have nothing bad to say really

AMAZING, again.. this game fascinated me on how they blend in cinematic and realism. The gun sounds so intense, the voice acting easily put most games to shame, they're just lfielike. They're just group of soldiers that fights for their life, their people, their family. And I question myself, Do I really that of a monster to kill those people?

There's nothing call as perfection, but near pefect, there certainly is, and this is the game. The Line is a game that everyone has to experience, It's a game that ask us a serious question to reflect, a series of phillosophy worth noting, and it tell us the cause and effect, action and consequences of war in a 'disturbing' way.

Spec Ops: The Line may seem like a typical military shooter at first, but it isn’t... not at all. 

Its strongest point, the story, makes up for every flaw that this game has. I won’t give you any other detail about it, with the exception that it is one of the most intense stories I’ve heard from a game and you just have to trust me and play through it. I don’t believe that there is any other game with such an unique plot and, in terms of how good the narrative is, it can be easily placed at the same level with other good story-driven games like The Last of Us and Alan Wake, which I highly recommend if you are interested in intriguing stories. Also, it is filled with lots of action, which makes it a good choice, even if you want to play something just killing some people, but, in my opinion, if you choose to play this game without paying attention to the story, you are simply wasting your time, as probably there are other mindless shooters out there which excel at this category. 

The cover system is pretty well done, even though your character will sometimes get into the wrong cover, which can instantly lead to your death if you are already being shot, especially on harder difficulties.  The AI of the squad mates sometimes made my enemies' lives easier, by going out of cover in critical situations and dying, which, combined with a hard difficulty, made it impossible for me to get my squad mate revived. Neither of the above is game breaking and, fortunately, these things rarely happen, so I can say that the gameplay itself is well polished. One thing I want to point out is that the enemy AI is pretty challenging, forcing you to take tactical approaches instead of getting out of cover and shooting everyone. Also, I feel that the sand mechanics were not used at their maximum potential and the developer could do much more with the idea.

The sound is another aspect of the game where it can be seen that the developer put a lot of effort.  The voice actors did a tremendous job, succeeding in making players easily cope with the characters. Fun fact: every single line of the script was recorded in just one day. You’ll probably think that the actors didn’t manage to do this without getting tired. Firstly, that’s the point: the developers wanted the voice acting to closely follow the game, which, with the help of the actors, they did. Secondly: you are talking about professionals. Should I mention that the main character is voiced by Nolan North, the one who was featured in games like the Uncharted series and The Last of Us? Also, the OST fits the game perfectly, giving you an adrenaline shot every time you find yourself in front of many enemies. (I have to admit that I’m into rock/metal music, but in my opinion, the music you’ll find in the game is best suited for this genre.)

The graphics are pretty amazing! Everything takes place in a post-sandstorm Dubai, which was very well represented by the developers. You get the opportunity to see a beautiful sight of the ruins of Dubai from one of its tallest buildings. Also, the great lightning effects and the attention to details makes up for some minor texture loading issues. There isn’t really anything else to complain about the graphics! I didn't experience any FPS drops, graphical artifacts or any other technical problems throughout the whole campaign.

So, if you are wondering whether to buy this game or not and it happens to be on sale, do yourself a favor… buy this game. I can assure you that you won’t regret it at all.

I'm going to be honest. Spec Ops the line is one of the most amazingly polarising experiences I've had.

On one hand, the gameplay is mostly generic and has your conventional third person shooter mechanics with occasional turret sections and the usual hoo-rah military gun porn one would expect of the genre.

On the other hand though, Spec Ops the line has a BRILLIANT and wholly original plot which not only seperates it from the endless stream of generic brown FPS games nowadays, but also had (or at least in my opinion) one of the best and most truly thought provoking plot twists I've encountered in recent memory. I dont want to spoil it obviously but what I will say is no matter what ending you get, much like Fallout New Vegas, you will feel like a terrible person.

This is a game where there is no clear cut line on morality and doesnt approach storytelling in the usual black and white way, where characters cant be labeled as simply good or evil. The great thing about the plot is that it makes you question the moralality of each character, including the protagonist and makes the plot almost imperative to reflect on.

It's just too bad the gameplay is just so uninspired and considering the games length it begins to feel long in the tooth really fast. I actually found myself bum rushing the last parts of the game after doing posisbly the 20th sniping section because I wanted to get answers so damn badly. Also the checkpoints near the end are f**king brutal to the point of frustration and many moments suffer from seeminly endless spawns of enemies (much akin to Modern Warfare). It's nasty.

At the very least I will give points to the game not skimping out on gore, to the point of nightmare fuel and it's use of sand as a major mechanic. Speaking of visuals, the game's art design is also VERY well done. The game leaves alot of very subtle hints about the narative through visual ques and colour filters, Once again I dont want to spoil too much but if your familiar with films like 'Synecdoche new york' you will notice what I mean.

In short, this is a game that despite it's frankly mediocre gameplay, has a plot and design execution worth discussing and reflecting on.

If you want to get past the gameplay, a lets-play is a worthwhile venture. Either way, check it out.

A title that deserves much more recognition than it has. I'd categorize Spec Ops: The Line as one of those games that everyone should play before they die. As many fans of the game will tell you, however, it's hard to explain my recommendation without spoiling the beauty of the game itself.

Gameplay-wise, there's nothing remarkable to write home about. The game is played from a third-person perspective, and unlike other shooters I've played, the controls feel awkward and clunky at times. The gunplay isn't terribly exciting and some confrontations tend to drag on for long periods of time, so I did find a lot of the fighting to be repetitive. The developers do throw some interesting dynamics into the mix that help keep things fresh, such as semi-destructible environments and the ability to issue minor squad commands. However, I could never recommend Spec Ops on its gameplay alone.

And I'm not. The main attraction--by far--is the plot, and it's why everyone should give this game a shot. Spec Ops delves deep into the questioning of morality and good intentions. It makes us question if we can define a side as "good" or "bad" in a given conflict, and it warns us of the potential repurcussions of acting on half-truths and speculation. At its surface, and for the first hour or two of the game, Spec Ops masquerades as a typical, generic military shooter. But by its end, it leaves us uncertain of even ourselves.

Spec Ops: [strike] The Line [/strike] The Feels is a gritty 3rd person shooter set out to put players through emotional torment as they question their actions while gunning down supposed allies. It's a relatively short game. You can finish it pretty quickly. It's a beautiful game. The graphics are excellent, especially the environmental effects. It's got some good squad-support mechanics, a bit of RTS mixed in when it comes to combat.

This is no CoD shoot-em-up against the russian/korean/middle eastern/chinese terrorists who pose a threat to MURRICA and the good guys have to go blast 'em with MUH FREEDOMS until they're all dead and a soaring bald eagle screams overhead just before the credits.

No, this game takes a much more realistic approach with a small squad in unfamiliar territory as you watch the effects of combat and decision-making on their mental state and relationships.

Of course, it's a game, so it is a dramatization. But it's an excellent game. Your choices have an effect. It wasn't made so you could choke on McDonald's while singing the Star-Spangled Banner. It was made to show that on the inside, there is no glory in war.

Gameplay?  Above average TPS à la Gears of War.  Solid, precise aim and feel.  Clunky-ish cover/vault/melee system, but effective enough that you won't die too much to it.  Two-weapon system, no real restrictions beyond ammo/grenade caps.  Fantastic world effects -- sand behind that window?  Yes, you can totally shoot it out and watch it knock an enemy over.

Execution?  Great.  Beyond the standard waves-of-enemies-then-move-on strategy, you have snipers to outsmart, and companions to instruct (that actually do what you ask -- most of the time).  There's a large quantity of particular scenes that are just wonderful.  The scene with a flashing light -- you'll know when it happens.  The scene where a sandstorm is pushing your team back, and you have to make a mad dash for safety.

But this game ins't amazing because of those.  It's amazing because of... well...

The story.  A terrifying morality simulator.  Absolutely wonderful character development.  A team you actually want to keep safe.  A common enem--wait, just kidding.  It absolutely smashes all the clichés you'd expect out of the genre and setting.  Actual choices that have quite an impact.

If not for some stupid issues -- blah graphics settings, horribly rigid control scheme, a tendency to just hang for no discernable readon, and some stupid  barricades with incorrect hitboxes -- it'd be one of the best shooters I've played.  Don't let those negatives detract you from this game, though.  Play it, if only for the story.

This game has a powerful plot that explores the rare spheres of PTSD, the horrors of warfare, and the definition of "good guys" and "bad guys."

You'll keep playing Spec Ops: The Line because of the characters; the way dispositions and reactions change, the way their voices break when they issue commands and pass on the battle picture, and the way they reply to your directions in a firefight.

I haven't played the multiplayer - I don't think there needs to be a multiplayer draw to this game at all.

If you enjoy good stories in games, you won't be disappointed with this one. There are different endings depending on what you do, although while it sounds contradictory, I felt railroaded at times.

If I had a major complaint, it would be the "execution" feature. If you approach a downed opponent, you can finish him off by beating him to death with your rifle or shooting him at point-blank. That's fine for Gears of War, but Spec Ops: The Line is about fighting actual people rather than one-dimensional, murderous aliens, and it's against the laws of armed conflict to attack wounded combatants like that. So it felt a little over-the-top during the game's early chapters.

If the coup-de-grace mechanic was introduced later into the game, during one of the more desperate late-game firefights, for example, I would have found it easier to swallow; it just seems like something more appropriate to the later stages of the game when everything has gone to hell and the protagonist's hands are already stained with more blood than he bargained for.

Why don’t you look at the suffering you just caused?" This game is not shy about making you look like a monster. There is a point in this game were you do something really, REALLY  bad, and when I had done that I needed to take a step back, turn off the game and remember it was all just a game and not real. But that part still sat with me lingering in my mind as I try to sleep that night. I did not play the multiplayer, but that’s not what I wanted this game for. This is a work of art, I have always enjoyed military shooters but this one really understands the psychological torment that can be inflicted to one’s mind in times of war. This game deserves a lot of recognition for what it accomplishes and a great step towards furthering games as an artistic medium.

Spec Ops: The Line... is the chest-high wall simulator (third person cover-based shooter) that I didn't expect to be good at all...

I'll admit, this game might not be as powerful as it was before I heard it played upon expectations of the player considering the cloning of CoD singleplayer campaigns, but it was powerful either way! Left me thinking for a long while about it, how you, the player, and the character you control are responsible for the actions in game, how traumatizing PTSD is, how war can be actually hell... I wrote this last one off of Capcom's big book of clichés... and that from Yahtzee...

Spec Ops: The Line tells you about a squad of three man who go into the city of Dubai that recently suffered a huge sandstorm. Before said enviromental hazard occurred, the 33rd Battallion was stationed there in order to organize an evacuation that failed. Your buddy characters are Alphanso Adams (the "aww hell naw" guy) and John Lugo (the cracka sniper) and the generic burly white dude captain is Martin Walker, who you'll be controlling! Along the way into Dubai, you'll venture into the terror of war, questionable choices and dive into confusing insanity. Right now you may be thinking: "shouldn't games be fun?". They can be, but what they also can also be simoultneosly or not, is compelling. Horror games aren't necessairly just fun, they're interesting due to their mystery and opression they give to the player. Such method is used by Spec Ops: The Line. Do you feel ok for performing the acts that the game tells you to do and should you feel guilty for doing them wheather you wanted to do it or not...? That you'll have to answer... the question is worth 70% of your grade...

Unfortunatly, I can't say much without spoiling the story otherwise from saying that it's fantastic and screws with your mind aside from some minor plotholes. I do love the choices you make in the game, instead of Mass Effect-style of: good, bad and neutral choices. Instead, you get grey and debatble choices that don't really lead to any happy ending and it's all done mechanically instead of a cutscene which I friggin' love it! The best way to transmit story in gaming is through mechanics since you yourself are in control of the character. There is no other medium that can accompish that! Some choices may not have an impact to the gameplay but at least they build up properley the illusion that they may have. What I feared about the game is that it would only develop its narritive through cutscenes rather through interactivity, but that wasn't true.

The plot twist is quite amazing, as good as that of Bioshock 1! If you haven't played that game, you should! It's one of those that you could've spotted it if you paid close attention to the story. The plot twist was so good that it desearved its own paragraph in my review!

The game left me very curious about it and I did some reasearch on it out of free will. There's a lot under this game and you know, this could be used for schools if games weren't considered "only for children". It's acessible in both of its gameplay and story, you get to explore many metaphors and secrets of the narritive at the same time. Certainly be better than a book that does not follow the rules of grammar even though for 12 straight years you've been taught to obey said rules but you'll still be forced to analyze said book because f**k you (the book is called: "Memorial dos Conventos"). Sorry, I just had to this a small rant.

As for the gameplay, like I said, it's a chest-high wall simulator. You regenerate HP, use generic weapons (that have good weapon feedback at least since they kick a lot), hide between cover so you can suck on your thumb while the screen cleans itself from all of the jam and use shemactical manuveurs to get an advantage over your enemy. You can use the tactical button to flash your enemies or frag them or have them eliminated by your team mate in one button. But these only appear in contextual situations. You also can revive them, but they can't revive you because REASONS! Or maybe there's as an actual secret reason towards it.

During the combat, you can also shoot down on your enemies: sand. However, this is rare and amist the tension of the combat, such traps will be easily avoided.

As for enemies, there's nothing much to hype about, you have the regular dudes, crazy psychos trying to stab you, shotgunners (nothing more annoying then a storm of bullets to your face), special shemelta squad troopers (that act the same way as the regular soldiers), snipers (aimbot hax!) and of course, JUGGERNAUTS (bullet sponge)! The plot twist to this is that you'll be fighting american soldiers who are just doing their job, they're just normal people that you'll be forced to kill. Overall, there are third person shooters that are much better than this like Mass Effect.

There are also stealth sections that require you to use your teamates to take out enemies immediatly without any trouble. But they're far too short and lack depth. I would like if they would extend but I guess it was their objective to make the game as generic as possible in order to shock the player later on. Still, I think it was already generic with its combat, so it'd be great if it could vary things up with the stealth sections. If this game was released nowdays in between the other games that have tacked on stealth, because developers can't think of anything else, then I guess the shock effect would be better pulled off assuming these stealth sections were longer.

You can also perform executions to finish off downed enemies, it's unecessary but looking at the enemy in pain whilst they're downed just makes you want to be merciful and take them out immediatly. The executions do become more violent along the way and if you play the game you'll know why...

Technically, it's a preety good PC port, it runs well, looks good, controls ok but there are issues. The explosions effects are really bad and the .ini files are encrypted. All issues can be solved with the PCgamingwiki. The game may be griddy and dark, but the bright yellow and orange colours have a lot of charm to it. It looks like both the visual aesthetic and the actual content itself contrast themselves. Finally, the lighting affects are preety good, but it depends on the filter you choose. Not sure why that's something important you have to choose at the start of the game.

There's also multiplayer which is preety much a desert town (get it... desert town... like Dubai...) and COOP which I have not tried yet. I don't think you'll miss much with multiplayer, even the dev said they didn't want it in the game but 2K ordered them to make a multiplayer mode.

In conclusion, this game will leave a mark in my memory and it'll surely leave one in yours. Do not spoil yourself with walkthroughs, you'll punish yourself from a good game with an actual good interactive  gaming experience! I recommend it!

Spec Ops: The Line boils down to being a game that ultimately used its mundane 3rd person shooter gameplay to its advantage to cause the player (you) to experience what the horrors of war can be like. 

You can read reviews and the plot of this game, but that is nothing compared to actually having to go through all of the decisions you make in the game and witnessing your own actions first hand. For me the turning point where I went from "okay this game is going like I read it to be and I'm not feeling that emotional kicker" to "oh man that was a little too much. I think they should've dialed that back. I feel kinda queasy just thinking about it. This is really absolutely properly depressing" around the halfway mark at which you are at a point of no return. Another thing that I really liked about this game are the multiple choices that you are presented in the game. There is no real right or wrong in the choices you make during the game, but I really appreciate tha the game developers allowed players to think outside the box, as I was able to make decisions opposite to what the game might psychology pressure you into doing (going into detail about what my decisions were to give a better example would unfortunately give major spoilers, but what I do feel comfortable in saying is that essentially you are able to make the more neutral decision in the opportunities the game supplies you so that you can be more merciful or morally on the high ground). 

I would like to say though, to ANYONE WHO HAS A HISTORY OF SEIZURE/EPILEPSY/ETC that can be brought on by BRIGHT REPEATEDLY FLASHING LIGHTS THERE IS A SHORT SEGMENT OF THE GAME THAT MIGHT TRIGGER SUCH MEDICAL ISSUES SHOULD YOU HAVE THEM and I would like to warn you of that as I don't recall the game ever warning the player of this during the beginning credits/startup. For anyone else WHO DOES NOT HAVE A HISTORY OF SEIZURE/EPILEPSY/ETC I would like to tell you that in a certain segment of the game *no your graphics card is not crapping itself* (as I personally thought it was when I first got to that level). It is simply put a really clever and creative way to drive home the dive into maddness so don't freak out when it starts happening.

I wish I could write a lengthier review, but I know that whatever I write won'd do any justice for the story of the game, it is simply something you have to experience yourself. The game play is like I said above really mundane and forgettable, and often times can be really annoying (it is a 3rd person shooter but not as refined or easy to control and navigate like Max Payne 3 was to give an idea to anyone with questions. I say this because I had trouble countless times getting into cover and shooting during the game in comparison to other games). While this was often times a source of major complaint and frustration while I played the game, I still really enjoyed the experience simply for that storyline. It is just simply put that powerful.

I bought the game during a Steam sale for what I believe was around $7 and I'd highly recommend this game at that price point. After you play this game you will end up greatly hating yourself as you watch a man spiral into insanity and question not only his decisions, but your own (during those decision opportunities I stated above).

AMAZING GAME! Visually stunning, trippy Apocolypse Now story line, and challenging enough at normal difficulty. This is one of those games you don't just play but expereince. Sounds lame, but if you've ever played that type of game you know what I mean. Couple things, though. Game mechanics leave a little to be desired. This game, like most shooters nowadays, blew right by me. I saw it as another military run-and-gun, storyless, dull, linear game. I was blow away by how mistaken I was when I picked this up on my PS3 about a year and a hlaf ago. First off, this game is hard as anything. A few shots and you're dead. Second, there was no enjoyment throughout my playthrough. In fact, there was only one time when I laughed and that was in the begining. Every single action I made just made me feel more and more ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Shooting American soldiers because I thought they were the enemy, burning them alive... Killing innocent civilians because they just happened to be there. This game is not a happy experience, however, it was the most compelling story, at least by a modern military shooter standpoint, that I had ever had the privlage of playing. Even with my second run with it, (which is why my hours are small) I was still shocked at the horror I commited whilst I rampaged through Dubai. It may have generic cover-shooter elements in it, but they are the focus of the game. It's the story and the "choices" you make throughout that are the focus. Even at $20, this is worth it. Even if you have no interest in cover shooters, play this. It is seriously the best army related game I have ever played.

The many people I heard telling that Spec Ops was a retelling of Heart of Darkness and Apocalypse Now weren't lying. It's exactly that.
The story, dialogues, design and voice acting are perfect.
Plus, for once, it's not just a game about glorifying war but about how war can screw people up real hard and real fast.

But I've got a serious problem with this game.
the "game" part.

I'm not big on TPS, I mean the only other TPSs I liked were Binary Domain (who had both a good story and decent gameplay) and Vanquish (0 story, all gameplay, all fun). But even like that i can tell you that Spec Ops is probably one of the most awful TPS, gameplay wise, ever made.
It's especialy true on FUBAR when you suffer the most from the clumsy control, stupid AI of our teammate and fake difficulty (The helicopter at the end of chapter 6, the enemies with unlimited grenade supply in chapter 13, the stupidly scripted fight in chapter 14, etc).

But still, even if there's not much "game" to play around, it's a great story to live and it is very well told.

PS : Don't bother with the multiplayer.

Well, I finished this game almost at once, so we can kinda say it sucked me in. Let's start with a little summary of the game.

Spec Ops: The Line is a rather linear TPS with a couple of places you can make your own decision between ♥♥♥♥, and even bigger ♥♥♥♥. And you'll feel ♥♥♥♥ in the end. 

The story:
Delta Force sent to Dubai for a recon mission that quickly turns into a rescue mission, then into a "shoot everything that moves" mission. It gets confusing at times, but the end (which I won't spoil you) helps. It's...not what you'd expect. You start out as your standard US Soldier shooter with the grizzled veterans shouting commands, shooting baddies, being badass, but that quickly turns around. You are just a piece of the chess game of the forces behind the scenes. To give credit to the game, the story of Dubai getting hit by sandstorms, and getting Fallout'd is rather cool. And the visuals match, but bit later about that.
Through the game I felt I was playing a TV series. Heck, it'd make a bloody good mini-series - about 6 episodes or so. The characters are good, and while not overdetailed, they do their job. And when I finished it, I felt like after a good TV show or movie. It left satisfied, but somehow empty. 
The conversions are awesome. I had a few laughs, but the interactions between the characters never went over the top, and kept me interested throughout the story. Nobody felt flat or uninteresting, so that's a pretty good thing too.
Overall, 8/10. I had little to no expectations, but left with something I won't forget soon.

Gameplay:
It's a rather standard TPS with a decent selection of firearms. You get Assault Rifles, Shotguns, Pistols, SMGs, LMGs, and so forth. Most of them has a secondary mode, which is to say switch the sniper rifle's zoom (from 8x to 16x), or put a sound suppressor to the M4A1. It's fun, and while the diversity forces you to either be a really accurate shooter, or switch your weapons frequently. Ammo boxes scattered around the maps help you. The cover system while sometimes tad awkward, is good. Made me think of Mass Effect. 
In every section you can find pieces of intels - a great way for knowing the backstory a bit better, and adds to the overall feel to the game. You'll be more disturbed after you find them fo' sure. Sometimes they are at obvious places, but you gotta look for the to find all.
The game is rather linear, but with a game like this, it's not much of a problem. I wouldn't list this as a pro, but neither as a con. It's just linear and that's it. 
7/10 - you'll remember the game for the story, as the gameplay is, while rather flowing, brings nothing new.

The visuals:
Like in my Sleeping Dogs review (which you probably haven't read, but I like to mention my other written stuffs), I have to state I don't have the full specifics to play the game on High graphics. I went with medium, and it ran with about 30 fps. For me, it's solid, and the game, while not gorgeous, it looked good. The Sandstorm'd Dubai (which is almost Darude, but let's stay away from memes for a second) looks good. It's pretty detailed, and I never got bored of the environment. It wasn't exactly the same as far as I recall, and fighting on the top of a skyscraper is a nice change after eating sand on ground level. It matched the game, so I'm fine with it as is.
Overall a 8/10.

Sounds:
Okay, this is awesome. The mad DJ with the hits of the 80s that he plays seemingly random, the ambient music, and the OST for the game is AWESOME. Fitting, believable, and you'll feel that it gives a lot to the game. You'll eventually search for the OST on Youtube, and save it to listen later. It's really good. Kudos to the composer.
10/10

Overall I'd give this game a 8.5 out of 10, totally worth playing, and totally worth your money. Be aware of the graphic images of gore, death, and the feeling of emptiness and guilt after you've finished the game, regardless of your choices.

*** SPOILERS ***

[spoiler]I feel like a total piece of ♥♥♥♥ once I was done with this game. No, really, I did. The game started out with a basic premise: go into a wrecked Dubai and secure an evacuation due to freak sandstorms. For some reason, the player also decides he's gonna go in a little TOO far. The name "Konrad" sticks like sugar water to the player once he hears him, and I'm given an enemy force that I truly believe was bad. Well, this is where it gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible, because I was killing my own soldiers including civilians and sure enough was just seeing the road to the protagonist's insanity.

Well, that happened to be true. The poor ♥♥♥♥♥♥ couldn't control himself -- he was literally a one man army hellbent on just killing this man no matter who got in his way. This bit him in the ass once he found out the man was dead, and he was just a psychotic mess from what he saw. With all his friends dead, he's unsure of his future now.

This game is a feelfest, and exposes many true horrors of war. Get it, and indulge yourself. You're in for a trip, and I don't want a sequel. I don't want to sit through this again, it was too depressing, true, and realistic. Humans are really capable of being heartless, cruel beings with a lack of empathy.[/spoiler]

Spec Ops: The Line is a decent game, but that is about it.

It has an untypical storyline compared to most other military shooters out there, which makes it stand out from the crowd.

However, gameplay-wise it is just your average cover-based modern military TPS. 
Dash to cover, shoot some enemies, change cover, rinse and repeat throughout the whole game.
Levels are 100% linear with nothing to explore. This means that replayability potential is practically zero, unless you want to get achievemnts or play on a higher difficulty.

You play some kind of mutant who has the ability to rapidly regenerate all of his health as long as the damage wasn't lethal, without the need of any kind of medical aid, but this is typical to most military shooters these days.

Game does pose a reasonable challenge on Suicidal difficulty, encouraging you to aim for headshots and conserve ammo, and there is also a FUBAR difficulty for true masochists which unlocks after you complete the game.

I haven't encountered any technical issues running the game on max settings, no noticeable fps drops or anything like that. There aren't any issues with mouse control as well. This is a big plus compared to how bad console ports big companies tend to release (Watch Dogs / Deus Ex HR / etc.) 

I think that this game is worth playing if you are even remotely interested, but it could have been a lot better.

As close to Dubai as you will ever get. 

Seriously though, this game is awesome. Not only is it pretty but fun as well. While there may be a few bugs and the running and cover system works well it could do with a couple small tweaks. Overall this doesn't really destroy the gameplay if you play the second lowest difficulty. I'm not sure about the higher difficulty levels. That level of difficulty should be good enough for seasoned FPS players.

There are a couple places where directions could be better but overall it doesn't ruin the gameplay except in one small spot that only takes about 1 minute to complete tops if you don't die.

The game is rather short (or regular length these days) at about 8 hours. The gameplay is fun, presenting you with several different situations. Where I think this game excells at is the moral choices you have to make. While some of these could be better presented as choices there are still several that are present as choices. It's been a while since a game has made me pause and think about a choice. This game did that. It has also made me ask if I made the right choice.

I strongly reccomend this game. The graphics are beautiful, the characters models are amazing, the sound and game play is good, and the strong moral choices you have to make this game what it is. Be prepaired to experince a fresh take on a war shooter.

There are 5 choices at the end of this game with a total of 4 endings. Each one leaves you in awe. This game is a mash up of the brutality of WaW, (a way better version of) the storyline of Black Ops, and the gameplay of Gears of War. The cover systems takes a little getting used to and the only real flaw are the sound errors that sometimes make the cutscenes silent. All in all, this game is a great gem that if you can pick it up for cheap on a sale, definately do so. 
Multiplayer is strange but OK imo.

I only played the story mode once and that was enough for me. still i recomend this game. because it takes the shooter concept and builds an intresting game around it.
I had some minor issues with the keyboard controlls and had to use to xbox controller to play the game. that was a minor problem i had. 
The fighting and combad mechanics where familiar and nothing to intresting. but the strong point for me in this game:

the story. i like how you get railroaded into more and more problems. I do not wish to poil but i going to tell, you will do bad things and it just makes me feel horrible. 

TL:DR: the combat was nothing to intresting but the story hanging around the combat scenes stucks to me and drives the point of the game home.

A game that will make you feel awfully bad about shooting people.

I personally liked a lot how the story unfolds, there are a moments in the game when it forcefully makes you stop shooting people and reflect about real warfare and all of its horrors. 

A very unique game with a strong message. Highly recomended.

10/10

GREAT STORY! It does well in dealing with topics such as PTSD and how war affects the soldiers. It does pretty well in showing that war might not always be a good vs. bad affair - there may also be a gray area within actions are made that while necessary are also detestable.

Cover system is great BUT there are times when I thought I was in a perfect spot to hide behind cover but the game doesn't recognize it and forces you to stand in open fire like an idiot trying to find the sweet spot by mashing spacebar to let you hide behind cover. The AI may also make stupid decisions such as rushing into the middle of a gunfight and getting incapacitated, but I didn't find this as bothersome as the cover system.

Still a great game despite its faults - as the narrative is worthy of being translated into film.

Just Finished this game. I originally ignored it thinking it was just one more standard military shooter, and I was very wrong about that. After playing it start to finish I can honestly say I haven't played a game this thought provoking in a long, long time.

Disclaimer: This game will make you feel like a horrible person.

But it really is a good game, magniflorious plot, decent realist difficulty, sadness. And anger... lots and lots of anger.

Like others have said, this is an incredible story that only gets better as you move through it. The characters grow and you're right there with them. The city itself is also ridiculously beautiful. You even get caught in dust storms at times, which is pretty cool.

The one thing I found occasionally frustrating is the sticky Sprint (which apparently is a feature, not a bug - kinda dumb). But the game/story is so good that, all in all, I'm really glad I put up with the mild annoyance.

It's really unfortunate that the game didn't do so well financially and the developers said they wouldn't make another like it for a while. The Line is a real gem. I hadn't heard about it until recently - hopefully if enough new people realize it's worth buying, the devs will have a change of heart. Then again, this game is so unique that I'm not sure it would work a second time.

Bottom line: Get it. If it's on sale, you really have no excuse. And stay away from spoilers!
Finally a really good ThirdPersonShooter with a good story. It's like the movie Apocalypse now, where more the story goes ahead, more the darkness inside the soldiers comes out, driving them crazy.

With very standard gameplay, this game excells in a compelling and conflicting story.
Spec Ops: The Line is a game for a certain taste.

SO:TL is a modern military third-person-shooter. It runs smoothly on my rig, and graphically, the game looks decent to stunning in some areas. The gameplay consists of very linear traversion of diverse environments in a war-ridden, half-destroyed dubai of luxurious architecture and skyscrapers. Often times, the leveldesign relies on simple cover-to-cover movement which unfortunately, especially on higher difficulties, feels more like camp-until-clear engagements, while adding in the componentof vertical gameplay and turret-sections. To be honest, it feels a lot like a cardboard-cutout of MM-shooters like CoD or Battlefields campaign gameplaywise. 
But if you feel like turning away from the game already from that, think again as the story of the game throws you in a sea of confusion and inner conflict. As the story progresses and the protagonists role becomes more and more influential, the game gebins to psych the player out of his skin, creating a surreal experience at times. The game comes in rough not to glorify the violence and gore on your account, and will make you feel guilty for everything you do like no game i've ever played before.
Although I considered quitting halfway through due to the bland gameplay, the ending was absolutely worth all struggle. The story told in this game is a reason to grab it anytime. I would recommend it anytime. 
8/10 would brown again

I feel that this game is extremely underrated and under-appreciated. Even if you're not a huge fan of cover-based 3rd person shooters, I would still recommend this game wholeheartedly. I enjoyed the gameplay and setting, but this game's strongpoint is, by far, the story. It examines war unlike any shooter ever has, and what you experience will stay with you for a long time. Spec Ops: The Line caused me to look back and quesiton the choices I made, and it induced an emotional guilt that very few other games have. 

Everyone who plays this game will have a lot to think about.

Note: This only covers the singleplayer expereince. I didn't play the coop or multiplayer. Look at the other review that talk about them. 

Pros:
+ Amazing story
+ Gameplay is fun
+ Graphics are pretty good (not amazing, but you can't really complain)
+ Nice voice acting
+ Multiple endings
+ The way your character changes over the course of the game is a nice touch.

Neutral:
+/- The AI isn't the best, but it works
+/- The gameplay can be a little repetitive. You take cover, shoot, and maybe throw a grenade. 

Cons: 
- It's pretty short
- [MINOR SPOILER] [spoiler] Some of the choices you make in the game don't actually affect the ending [/spoiler]
- Not a fan of the controls
- I don't like how you die. When you are killed everything goes into slow motion and slowly fades to black. Then before it goes to black it says "You Are Dead" in blurry white text. It's not very dramatic. This is something that really only bothers me so feel free to disregard this.

Conclusion:

Highly recommended game, but I wouldn't get it for full price if i only wanted it for the singleplayer.

Despite a few hiccups in the narrative, the story alone makes this game worth playing - however in my experience the gameplay doesn't hold up all the way through the game and you might find yourself holding on just to see the story progress. 

Expect to get at least 5-6 hours worth of single player gameplay here so purchase with that in mind. It runs pretty well and I had no major technical issues on my machine despite it being a console port. You'll need to sort out mouse acceleration too but it also plays well on a controller.

One of the best war games I've ever played. I've always wanted to play a game that showed the darker/real side to war so, when I heard about Spec Ops: The Line I was very interessted. It exceeded ALL expectations. I regret every decission I made in this game and everytime I think about it I remember just what a horrible person I am. This game completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ me up and I feel everyone should experience it. 10/10

I almost want to be  upset that the game was a bit shorter than I expected, but with how good it was I feel like complaining about that would be even worse than the things I did in the game. Hands down one of the greatest, and most unique, stories I have experienced in a video game in awhile. 

It asked questions that needed to be asked, ones that take a toll on the main character as well as leaving a powerful impact on the player with the unspeakable choices and forced, unavoidable situations. The combat was fairly solid, reminded me more of Gears of War in terms of mechanics than anything. 

All in all, I would buy it again, and at full price too. Don't let this game slip under your radar.

For starters the gameplay is good. Not bad, not amazing, good. 

The gameplay consists of taking cover, popping up, shooting, throwing the odd grenade and killing your way to the next location. Yea, a few things are stiff at times but it makes some decent use of enviromental objects, the weapons feel pretty good and it's a decent challange. 

The real reason you want to play this game is the story. It's not really story about war but the story of a slow, spiraling slip into insanity, parnoia, distrust and breakdown of a small group of main characters over the choices of the main character. 

Not spoiling anything because the story is too good to do so but it even leads to the odd feeling of distrust and disconnect between you and the main character as he does more and more that just seems compleatly out of your control. No matter what you do you cannot stop him as he keeps going to achive his goal and you almost grow afraid of what he will do next in order to achive said goal. 

If you just want to shoot things and are not intreseted in the story don't bother. 

If you want a story that will make you have to think, feel and that will stay with you days and even weeks after play Spec Ops The Line.

This game was the biggest emotional ride ive ever taken in a videogame. The stereotypical gravely voiced protagonist made me actually care about him by actually questioning his actions. Most games dont show the emotions for all the people who are slaughtering (instert american enemy here). This game showed some of the true horrors of war and i love it for that. Be prepared to feel like you had just been punched in the face by the ending. I do wish it was longer than 7 hours tho.

One of the best shooter/true war games I've ever played. It's not long, but every single minute of the game takes you thru a journey of this dark, thematic story. I highly recommened this.

PROS:

- Good Voice Acting to the T

Cons:

Play it now! It's cheap, too! $7.50 sometimes on Sale. Enjoy

Revisited recently and holds up very well - Interesting also to see how prescient this title was for storyline with many other similar stories across all other media types now being told - Ahead of it's time

An enjoyable game with a good story. Certainly not the best shooter out there by any means, but it's probably one of the best narritive's I've seen in a shooter. The gameplay is your standard TPS and controls well. One of those games that last just long enough to not outstay its welcome (clocked in at 6.2 hours for me to complete it). The multiplayer is absolutely guff (and dead) - there is also a co-op mode that I never tried.

Worth £20? Probably not, but this game is often on sale for about £5 or less - at that price it's a steal - buy it and play it over the course of a day or two, and get engrossed in the story.

This was a well written game.  But this was not a fun game.  We can give it high marks for controversy and other stuff expected out of a movie, but if you're looking for something enjoyable, this isn't it.  You can never win and every choice makes sure that you lose in some way or another.  There are no ways around it and the setup is very linear making sure that you cannot escape having to make a bad choice one way or another.  Installed it after a few hours.  Wasn't worth the time to finish it and the funnelling into having to make choices is a load of crap.

If you want to be frustrated thorought the entire game then this is for you.  The FPS aspect is mediocre and not very fulfilling so it won't help you along.  The storyline is fairly..meh.. with several cliches and  plotholes which can be ignored but really shouldn't.

If you want a game that you will enjoy, this don't get this game.  As well written as it is, it's not an enjoyable experience. This isn't gritty.  This is agonizing.

Wow. I didnt expect much from this game other than another shooter i'll regret buying. This is far more than what I expected. The ending in this game is awesome and unique. You'll be questioning everything once you complete the game.

I dont even know what to say about this game, where do I begin? I had never heard of it before but thought I would take a chance based on the reviews and could not pass up the deal Steam was having on it. Let me just say that I cannot even begin to say how much I loved this game. I will play this game over again making different choices to see how it will turn out going other paths. This game is dark and you will hate yourself for playing it, but you will not be able to stop as you will have to see how it ends like I did.

for me its a 10/10 because of its great story and voice acting.

If Heart of Darkness were to meet a third-person fps then Spec Ops: The Line would be the love child from that relationship. Nice combat, good story, and it gives a real look on how morality plays into modern wars.

Do you feel like a hero yet ?

It is a crime that SO: The Line is way under the radar. Hands down, it is one of the best third shooter games I've ever played. This is not another one of those shooters were you go all out Rambo on your opponents' asses in the name of Mighty 'Murica.

The story is something else. I went through a lot of mixed feelings while playing it ranging from anger, to disgust, to regret. The story features multiple decisions to make, which neither will be good or bad. 


The graphics are pretty and the setting of the game is unique. Despite being a work of fiction, it actually gave me sorta of an answer to my question which is; how would a post apocalyptic Dubai look like ?


Now for the gameplay. While many people found the gameplay to be average, I actually loved it, probably because I love third person shooters such as Killswitch (regarded as the godfather of 3rd person shooters, Uncharted, TLOU, Gears and many others. Aside from shooting, running, and hiding, you get to order your unit to either take down targets, stun them, heal an injured comrade or "revive" him if he is down.

This game is a must play. Don't judge it from sh!tty screenshots or youtube videos. Try, at least, the demo and judge for yourself.

Summary: mediocer and short third person shooter with a plot that made me actively despise it.
1. as third person shooters go, this isn't the best. The gun play and cover mechanics didn't feel fluid they felt cumbersome. Just play mass effect instead. 3/5 for third person mechanics

2. as far as story goes, it's prety bad. Over and over again the game makes refference to the heart of darkness and in many ways the game is an alegory to said book. The problem is that spec ops the line's story really doesn't hold a candle to heart of darkness. Long story short, If you've got the 6-8 hours it takes to play this game, just read the book. 1/5 for story.

3. building on 2, the plot seeks to make up for its weakspots and short comings and lack of any depth or meaning by throwing in a bunch of messed up stuff. This makes the game very dark which a number of people seem to have confused with quality and depth. It's not, it's just really messed up. 1/5 for making me feel terrible for playing it.

Amazing game. Accomplishes more in just six hours than some games do in three times that. A psychological thriller that depicts the struggle of a US Army Captain and his squad in Dubai. Characters are very dynamic which makes the story much more interesting and the graphics are very nice on Ultra settings. Well worth your time and money

Spec Ops: The Line seems like any other military shooter or Gears of War clone. And comparing only the gameplay, it is. But the story - or better the portrayal of the setting - sets it apart.

In Spec Ops: The Line you play Cpt. Walker, the leader of a three man squad that enters an evacuated Dubai that has been flooded by sand. Your mission is to investigate about a missing American Battalion and its leader. What starts as seemingly standard premise for a game soon turns into Apocalypse Now as the lines between enemy and ally become blurred.

In military shooters I admit that I usually don’t stop and think to why these armed people are shooting at me and who they actually are. The game usually never forces the player to reflect on that. The Line takes breaks in between and the squad discusses questions like: Who is the enemy that just popped up? A resistance against foreign influence? Rogue american soldiers? Why are they fighting you? Couldn’t you stop this blood-shed?

Soon some scenes pop up that force you to choose in one way or another, and the consequences are never foreseeable. Get intel from an important agent or save civilians instead? And this is just an easy example.

Harder decisions not only weigh on you but also on the protagonist and your squad. Cpt. Walkers battle comments get more frustrated, your squadmates follow your orders less if they lose trust in you. This is the kind of reflection on actions I wanna see in titles that show war - the most terrifying thing on this planet.

I salute Spec Ops: The Line for going this way, it shows that military shooters can still hold depth and be relevant and intelligent as well as ask important questions. The gameplay itself is quite linear and plays smooth, nothing that hurts flow much, but also nothing outstanding - simply solid. Having even more consequences to your actions a la The Walking Dead would make the impact feel even stronger, maybe for the next tour.
At first you'll love the game. Then you'll hate the game. Finally, you'll realize that actually you end up hating yourself while you try to pin the blame on mankind. 10/10

The story starts off pretty simple and straightforward, but slowly reveals the layers and characters that are involved in the chaos that permeates throughout Dubai. I found myself hooked from the beginning as Captain Walker's squad is constantly trying to get some understanding and control of what is happening around them. I can't remember what chapter, maybe 10 or 11, but Colonel Konrad said something that for the first time ever in a third or first person shooter did I find myself questioning if the decisions and path I had been taking was the right one. Spec Ops: The Line has the best story of any game I've ever played, and I'm not saying that lightly. It sucks you in with a growing sense of confusion, then as soon as you think you have it figured out, that its just like any other game, and the hype was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it hits you with more mystery than ever. Although the story takes place entirely in post sandstorm-ravaged Dubai, the various levels are totally different in feel and atmosphere, and run the entire spectrum from long range sniping on windy rooftops, to sand filled buildings, down to dark and wet cramped tunnels. The ending is heartwrenching, and will make you feel horrible about yourself.

The gameplay is exciting and fast paced, and requires a steady, measured level of aggression that puts you much closer to the enemies than most other shooters. Cover is vital to survival, and the controls, being designed around that concept, feel very fluid once you get used to them. This game gives you everything you could want in a military shooter: stunning setting, increasingly difficult enemies with a great AI, convincing characters, stunning setting, variety in weapons, a loading screen that starts off with helpful hints but eventually mocks you, stunning setting, absolutely amazing music, an amazing epilogue level, stunning setting, a very "fairy-tale-esque" structure that makes you into a shining hero.... 

Did I mention the setting is stunning? There are moments when you simply have to take a moment from shooting, just to admire the scenery. Or, if not admire, at least... observe. Some of the locations are gruesome on their own, and with context become downright horrifying. But the majority of the game imbues a sense of ruin and desolation in a place that was, until recently, almost unreal in its luxery and beauty. 

The game paints a picture of humanity's darkest side, and will make you question the moral implications of the very existance of military shooter games such as this one. Its rated M and they damn well mean it. Everything about this game is brutal, and may have given me mild PTSD. By the time you finish the game, you will have most certainly crossed The Line.

The TL;DR short summary (scroll down further for long review):
Pros:
+Incredible single player story. It is thought-provoking and very refreshing. This is what you're playing this game for. Did I mention the story is amazing?
+The decisions you make, aside from being very morally ambigious and "there is no good choice", are actually pretty creative in that the game does not tell you WHAT you can choose. It plays both on the minds of the characters as well as YOU, as a player.
+Decent gameplay. Standard 3rd person shooter with cover system.
+Using sand as a gimmick mechanic adds a little originality to the title. There is also a little bit of tactical squad use (ordering your squadmates to do things) that is limited, but works very effectively and keeps the game from being too boring.
+Great music, very fitting for the game. A few well-known bands are in there, such as Hendrix, but the original score is not too shabby either.

Cons:
-Fairly generic gameplay (It's good, just not great or bad. To be honest you can't really innovate modern warfare without getting all ridiculous though).
-Co-op is available but only in the form of challenge modes, not in the campaign. Multiplayer is also available but not worth it. You're playing this for the story!

Spec Ops: The Line is a terribly dull title and has a "seen that before" cover art. But don't judge a game by its cover, as it contains some truly entertaining and thought-provoking storytelling that is sadly rare in the shooting genre these days.

Taking place in Dubai, the worst sandstorms in history hit the region, stranding many civilians. The "Damned 33rd" infantry battalion of the United States Army is sent in on relief duty, led by a famous Colonel named John Konrad. However, it appears he and his unit deserted; they disobeyed orders to abandon the city, and the sandstorms effectively create a 'wall' that prevents surveillance and communications, essentially making Dubai a 'no man's land' where no one knows what's going on. You play as Captain Martin Walker, who is sent alongside two fellow soldiers as Delta Force operators for reconaissance. The mission is simple: Confirm the statues of Konrad and any other survivors, then radio for extraction.

As officially stated by the game's advertisement/captions, the story is very rich and takes plenty of influence from the novel "Heart of Darkness", as well as the movie "Apocalypse Now". Without spoiling this game any further, I can say it lives up to the hype. Your progression throughout the game will have you feeling disgusted, but not in the same in way a bad game would. As you delve deeper, you will see things you rarely see in video games - Among the list includes horrific imagery, morality, questionable actions, tough decisions and more....

It starts off innocently enough, almost like every other shooter out there. America coming in to save the day, foreigners shooting at you, nothing you haven't seen before. Next thing you know, the line gets very blurry and there are no "good" or "bad" guys, no "good" or "bad" decisions. By the time you enter the credits, you're left looking at war in a different way, and thinking about the actions and consequences of people.

In addition, the little touches are pretty awesome. Be sure to take breaks frequently and see how the main menu has changed throughout your progression of the campaign. Take in the environmental storytelling (additional "stories" you observe by looking at things not necessarily important to the main plot). Pick up glowing objects ("Intel") to reveal additional story threads. And DEFINITELY pay attention to the loading screens - they are plenty of them and they...well, let's just say if you're too good at the game, it's worth purposely dying multiple times to see them.

Also among my favourites from this game are the creative decision-making you'll have to make. The decisions you make, aside from being very morally ambigious and "there is no good choice", are actually pretty creative in that the game does not tell you WHAT you can choose. In fact, it doesn't make it obvious at all - there are no buttons or signs pointing in a direction. Without spoiling much, it offers commentary both on the insanity of war and the characters themselves, but also how you as a player may have been trained to think or behave in video games.

As for the gameplay, it's decent. It's a somewhat generic 3rd person shooter with a cover system. You take cover, shoot, reload, all that jazz. What makes the gameplay a tad more unique is their sand and tactical command mechanics. In various locations, sand can be used to your advantage - for example, shooting out windows behind enemies to break the glass and release a wave of sand that will blind or bury your foes. As for tactical commands, you learn how to use your squadmates more effectively by giving them simple orders. In most cases, all you can do is line up the reticle and tell them to target someone, and they'll focus fire him. However, the squad AI is fairly smart (and actually not invulnerable, which is nice) and will use grenades to take out entrenched foes, and sniper rifles for long ranged attacks. Various times the game will also allow you the option of telling them to throw flashbangs to stun foes.

In addition the game does come with co-op and multiplayer features, although these generally are not worth it. Co-op might be fun if people ever want to revisit Spec Ops, but these are limited to challenge modes, and not the campaign. A bit of a downer as I can see co-op gameplay working well in the story, but nevertheless it does make sense to exclude it. As for multiplayer, as you may have seen from other reviews it's pretty much not worth it. There are better games out there for multiplayer shooters, not to mention the population of Spec Ops multi-players is likely non-existent.

To conclude, play this game for the story. You won't regret it, although you'll certainly feel something by the end of the story. I do not recommend playing this so close to Christmas time like I did - it's kind of the opposite of happy feelings.
