Play this game. You may regret it, but it is a game that everyone who like shooters needs to play. I was confused, I felt like ♥♥♥♥, I didn't know what was right, and I felt emotions that I didn't know I had. I cannot recommend it enough.

This game, will make you think twice of what you are and what you do (in the game, maybe in reality but lets not push it that far). 

This game make appear to be another modern shooter where things all go to hell and only one country (*cough* america *cough*) is there to be the hero that save everybody, which it is not the case for this game.

 Without giving away the story or plot of this games.  unlike most first-person and 3rd person shooters. That make you feel like an bad ass one man army who can wipe an entire country  in a blink of an eye if you wanted to, no. This game shows you the dark side of what it means of being at war, for being a soilder, for being a human.

For gameplay its a 3rd person shooter and the controls are great, never had a problem except with one mission (but i assume its a one time deal so it wouldn't effect the gameplay or my recommendation of this game). 

Voice acting is good and does have rememerable characters that each voice actor protrase as..

I love this game. I'm new to PC gaming and my steam library is a little small because I'm a picky player. This game has kept me entertained for hours. Deffinitly a recommend and will be buying all future DLC.

First time reviewer, but I had to write a review for this Excelent hidden-gem game!
The game mechanics is like gears of war, third person take cover and shoot.

Positives:
Excellent, mind-blowing story that will keep you at the edge of your seat.
Non-stop action packed gameplay.
Dark atmosphere
Great enviroment (post-apocalyptic Dubai)
Multiple endings

Negatives:
some problems with the cover mechanics
Linear gameplay

BTW, this review is after I have completed the campain.

Finally an action game with a worthy storyline that keep you interested!

I give this game easily 8/10, HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!

I love games that make you think. Even more I love games that make you feel. As you might have read before, this game is an average third person shooter (at best). Although it was meant to be so much more. Just the concept of its story telling is reason to invest your time in this game. Spec Ops: The Line shows you the brutality of war. It shows you you the insanity of conflict. However,  it does not only shows you, it mocks you, if you decide to play on. It asks you with each step. "Are you ready to stop playing now?" And with every positive answer it rewards you with another brutal experience. 

Many are angered that it doesn't give you a choice, but punishes you for doing things that are scripted, that you had no way to avoid. To that I say: "That is the point of this game." Not only that, it gets harder and more brutal to carry on, the game itself just starts to oppose you. In the beggining, on loading screen you might see some helpfull tips, but as the story goes on, the same loading screens start to remind you what horrible things you did.

10/10 will not play again.

The games story and the idea to show war in all its cruelty is good and new idea for a shooter. Graphics and sound are also very well and blend in well with the atmosphere the designer wanted to create. However this game suffers from one big flaw that in my eyes make it kind of unplayable for  people who want to play this game on PC. It suffers heavily from consolitis. You feel all the time that it is meant to be played with a gamepad and not with mouse and keyboard. I am not a console hater but if you want to publish a game on pc as well than put enough effot in it so can be played in proper way. There other games like GTA IV which showed that it is possible to do so. Bad controls destroy the good concept and in any other very well crafted aspects of thisn game.

Overall a very good game. Starts out slow but picks up very quickly as you make your way through ground zero. Despite the clunky controls the game is really solid and makes you conserve amunition. Parts of the story really make you question your morality and there are plenty of OMFG moments that will suit your Micheal Bay needs. Hats off to the devs for making such a work of art. The multiplayer though is lacking as it was tac'd on at the last minute at the publishers demand so don't play it. If you have extra money then do yourself a favor and pick this game up. 4.5/5

Brilliant brilliants brilliant. A few moments seemed like oversight in the story and give a conflict of meaning, but over-all this is the most impactful and powerful generic third person shooter you will ever play. Let me put this straight. The fun isn't in the gameplay. The guns get boring, fights are stale, and there's practically no variation. However, the meaning of this game isn't to be fun. It's to fatigue you. To exhaust you and just want it all to end. I would hate to spoil this game, but just know, that the main hook here is story. You'll go through that grind, just to know what happens at the end. To find out what this entire game is even about. And trust me, you won't be dissapointed when you find out. This game will take you on a real experience, mandatory for anyone like me who sees modern military shooters like CoD as brainless shooting gallaries.

The true reality of war in a game. Spec Ops The Line captures it all, the death defying stunts, the psychological pain, and the comradery between brothers in arm. BEST GAME EVER, will never find one like this.

Very good game, starts like a 3rd person shooter, then you start getting into the story and you forget the shallowness of this "shoot'n'kill" genre. Voice acting is awesome, the story, very deep and will make you hate war and yourself.

More 3rd person shooter like this should be made.

Totally recommended.

At first sight when you never play this game to the very end; small levels with quite linear gameplay so a normal rail shooter by today’s standards, worth a look if you like the shooter genre (as you can tell I am not a fan of the genre)
When you finish the game: The story just changed everything and makes you think the game is epic because of very unexpected changes.

I really enjoyed this game because I hate your typical mainstream hero shooter game with 0 relation to the real horror of warfare. This game emerged me so much I played it from start to end in 1 day a rare thing for me. 
Your 2 AI companions are surprisingly smart, rarely had to save them from a stupid action + I can order them to focus on my target and I experienced 0 bugs. I only talk about single player but there seem to be a few co-op missions and multiplayer for which I (and most players) did not care.

Graphically it was great, the choices and rare use of environment are appreciated but don't mean or change much. The story is the big plus for this game and was well executed. There are no good guys in this game only realistic humans. Wish there were more shooters like this but with more meaningful choices and bigger levels.

At the discount I bought it, definitely recommend it. I never recommend shooters at full price they don’t last long enough and offer little replay ability in this case maybe once for a special difficulty, some collectables and the different endings.

One of the most underrated shooters ever, awesome storyline makes you truly think about some of the horrors of war. Literally felt sick for about 1/4 of the game. Amazing ending and multiple choices well worth playing

I see a lot of hate, and bashing on this game. I can see why. Before I go any further, let me give you a run down of the Cons.

Lets start with the control's. To put it bluntly, they're... pretty crap. I found myself not running when I want to, not sliding into cover when I want to, popping out of cover for some odd reason and not being able to hit anything when I've clearly shot something.

As for gameplay. It's mediocre, though not bad. It's basically.... Gears of War, straight up. Executions, how the cover works, even the crossair's look incredibly similar at some times. I haven't touched multiplayer, so I can't really say anything but all I've heard is how awful it is. I can believe it. A game like this... it just doesn't work well with the whole PvP scene. Graphics are typical PS3/Xbox360 stuff. On the other hand the Leveldesign, though linear, is well made and creates a atmospheric and breathtaking environment I often found myself starring at in appreciation. 
AI is decent. Squadmates are actually useful, taking cover and supporting you. Enemy AI will use suppressive and cover fire and try to flank you and also use grenades to flush you out of cover.
Not gonna talk about MP. Yager studio themself said in an interview they didn't want it and they didn't do it. But Publisher 2K still made a different studio do it and shoe-horned it in...
So what is the BIG selling point of this game? It's narrative!

If "Apocalypse Now" (and for that matter "Heart of Darkness") was a game, this is what it would be like. You will see plenty of references and parallels but rest assured, the game isn't just a copy. It has a story in its own right and goes its own ways.

As the story unfolds the lines between good and evil will start to dissolve until there is nothing left. You are being dragged into a conflict you have no concept off and always left one step behind. It keeps spiraling out of control fast as things turn sour and ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan - mainly because of your own ignorance - while you also have to bear the dire consequences of your actions.

On the metalevel the game is toying with alot of our preconceptions about Shooters, how violence and morality is represented and going into some other really deep stuff if you start thinking about it.
SpecOps deliberately keeps giving the players red herrings, false targets and vague objectives and watches us kill again and again regardlessly. It says we need to blow up some people and we do it. 
Because it is what needs to be done to accomplish the mission, right?  "We have no choice" like Cpt. Walker says. After all we are the good guys, fighting for a just cause with only the best intentions. Violence is a mere necessity. 
Who would have thought those people might be unarmed civilians with children? And at the next loading screen you will be asked  “Do you feel like a hero yet?”
That effectively is what SpecOps is all about: to ♥♥♥♥ with your head and expectations. This game is a mind ♥♥♥♥ through and through.

Bottom line: don't let yourself be put off by it's looks, because there is more to it than it first seems. You should really give it a try! Chances are you won't be disappointed.

Despite the misgivings of this somewhat thought provoking game being mired down with the requirements of a modern video game, I recommmend it. Sure, the game isn't as gripping as Conrad's novel or Apocalypse Now, but it's a pretty damng good display of "the horror".

Something that can truly be eye-opening. Spec Ops: The Line is one of those hidden trasures that comes along now and then. It's nice to see the AAA community try something different, and Spec Ops does just that and led me to many surprises one after the other.

It is easy to mistake this as some bad Call of Duty clone at first glance. I thought the same when I first saw it and I'm confident I'm not the only one. To avoid spoilers I will talk about what goes on in the game as little as possible, but there are certain subjects the story of Spec Ops: The Line touches on that throws a bit of the harsh realities of war into the face of the player.

I have talked to many soldiers, both currently active and those who were active. There is a consistent theme: there is no moral high ground in war. Spec Ops delivers on this very well. You are constantly given moral choices that don't seem to have a positive outcome either way, and you're constantly making decisions based off incomplete information, and it just sends things further spiraling downward to create the story masterpiece that is Spec Ops.

Since I can't talk more about the story without giving things away, you should stop reading this and buy Spec Ops now.

You play as a soldier fighting the good fight, fighting to save people and set them free from oppression. You, dear player, are the hero. Only you're not. The game helps you question why we obey whatever directives we are gives in any FPS. Why do we shoot these people? Are they all bad? Are we so morally superior that whoever we shoot is always the bad guy? Well, I suppose shooting people who are shooting at me is a pretty good way of staying alive. Fair point. But what about people who are not shooting at you? Spec Ops: The Line plays with your sense of self in a game and the fact that you identify with the character you play. 

On the gameplay side of things (I did buy the game before it appeared on Steam), it does not play as smoothly as say a Call of Duty. However, whatever gripes anyone might have with weapons handling, it does not subtract significantly from gameplay in general.

There is nothing I can say any better than what has already said about this game.  The game mechanically is generic; a third-person shooter with some squad based combat with the added bonus of using the world around you as a means to fight, this being done thanks to the sandstorms and the trapped sand within the enviornments themselves.  

Glass can be shot to cause an avalanche of sand to smother your enemies, or simply to blind and disorient while you go in for the kill.

But that isn't why it is mandatory that you play this game.

The narrative and everything used to frame it, even the very "generic" layer of the game is all done with the intent to drive home a story that while far from original (it is loosely based off of the novel, Heart of Darkness) has never been more personal.

This is easily the best version of the story I have ever come across, because while the movies and the books that portray it have done well and moved on to become classics, this is a version that is going to make it personal for you.  This is a version that is going to make you care, a version that will haunt you long after you finish it.

It is a game that will forever alter your perception of both what video games can be and what they already are.  

I feel that this is a game everyone should play.  It doesn't matter if you turn it on easy mode, it doesn't matter if you simply cheese your way through the levels, I don't care.  The narrative is there, it is strong and it is going to grab you by the throat and force you to look into a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mirror.  If I had my way, I would purchase every copy of this game and give it to anyone with the capablity to process a narrative. 

It is that damn powerful.   Do not cheat yourself by skipping out; buy this the moment you can. 

Than, lock your doors, close your windows and put on some headphones for a few hours.  Just brace yourself, because you're going to experience a story not as a soldier, not as a gamer...but as a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ human being.

You play the leader of a small squad tasked with trying to find a general believed to still be alive somewhere in a ravaged Dubai. As the story progresses you are faced with some plot changing ultimatums which will have an impact later on, the more you get to these stages of the game the more you are drawn into this world and the story itself.

If you can set the detail level and textures to max on your PC, then i strongly advise to do so. So many times i'd completely forget about the objective and just stop and look around in awe at the strange mix of a half destroyed metropolis, really quite impressive considering it was released a few years back.

Difficulty is actually quite challenging and can be brutal in some places, it's a fairly short game but dying so many time got a bit more longetivity out of it. For all the talk about games as art few AAA titles really aim to be more than entertainment, the equivalent of Summer Blockbusters that fill the screen with gorgeous visual set-pieces but fail plots or characters more developed than those of mustache-twirling villains plotting for power for powers sake (see Call of Duty Kevin Spacy for reference).

Spec Ops the Line plays with these conventions amazingly; a few levels in and it's a typical (competent but not outstanding) cover-based shooter with a niche trick of having sand as a usable environmental weapon. As it progresses it becomes so much more; a critique of war, of making a game of war, of people who 'play' at war, of nationalism and the idea of right and wrong when it comes to ending life in all sorts of circumstances.

To discuss the plot directly would be to undermine the power of progressing through the narrative oneself and I'm forever grateful that this is one experience I got to have spoiler-free. I can't say it was pleasant, but I can say I'm grateful to the developers and writers for not backing down and following the story to the conclusion it needed. If the 'Call of Duty' and 'Battlefield' franchise are 'Boy's Own' comics then this is 'All Quiet on the Western Front'.

It doesn't need multiplayer and it really doesn't need the 'Spec Ops' title-prefix, it does need support and wider recognition, and it's something I recommend for anyone who who considering a military career as a result of their CoD-obsession.
A must play for anyone who has played a any shooter game. It really makes you think about how you look at those games and the nature of escapism with violence.

The debate of "Games as Art" has been raging for as long as any gamer can remember without any sort of certain or definite answer. Well, if one thing is certain, it's that if games are art, then Spec Ops: The Line is Dada. It is anti-art. It is that which kills art. It is the destroyer.

From early on, the game makes this clear. It takes every trope and cliche from modern-based military themed shooters and turns them completely on their head. Instead of shooting anonymous brown-faced people, you're shooting Americans. Instead of watching your character suddenly evolve from a basic-fresh recruit into an elite badass soldier, you watch your character gradually devolve from a level-headed everyman soldier into a bloodthirsty and delusional psychopath. Instead of having bottomless reserve of neverending 5.56 NATO rounds for your M4A1 Carbine with which to mow down legions of enemy soldiers, you get just enough ammo to contemplate saving a bullet for yourself. Instead of moral choices, you make immoral choices. Instead of choices at all, you are given none. Instead of enjoying yourself and being inspired by the game's story and message, you'll find yourself suffering through it until you're caked in blood and dirt, kneeling over the toilet and attempting to retch up what little remains in your stomach.

Instead of encouraging you to keep playing, the game informs you, quite early, that the only correct response to all of this is to turn off the game and stop.

   "No... This is wrong! We did this part already!"

In terms of gameplay, The Line is in every way, shape, and form the definition of a generic third-person cover shooter. There is nothing to be surprised about here. It could be argued that this generic playstyle is integral to communicate the game's message, but it could also be argued that the game attempts to, as RPS put it, have its cake and eat it too. I will break this review into 3 parts; Gameplay, Graphics, and Story.

GAMEPLAY
The gameplay is coverbased, thirdperson. Similar to Gears of War, but not quite the same. I was glad to find that this game didn't do what most games fo when they want to make themselves more difficult. That being giving baddies more hp and more DPS. It only takes a single dirrect burst to drop most baddies (save armoured heavies encountered later in the campaign) and same goes for you. YOU ARE NOT BULLET PROOF! nor can you carry thousands of rounds of ammo, you have to conserve and make shots count. You need to take cover in order to survive, and the cover system is fluid after you get the hang of it. The game uses the setting of desert storms to allow you some environmental effects. You can shoot out windows piled up with sand to burry enimies, knock out glass floors when your on top of a building, and more besides. It is used often enough to matter, but not enough to become a gimic.

GRAPHICS
These are nice enough, for when they were made. Because of the desert setting, extra attention is paid to color and lighting. It has amazing effects for the story. Animations are exelent with one exeption: the main characters face. It does not match the voice at all which is a shame because the voice acting is exelent, and even in cinematics, remains wooden and lackluster 
As the story progresses, the colors textures, models, and even the voices, change to accomidate the story, to great effect I might ad.

STORY
This is NOT an action shooter. It is in fact, a "horrors of war" game. Now it is Very difficult to pull off a Horrors of War MOVIE without it turning into action-porn, and conveying the war drama effect in a GAME is downright impossible. But these guys DID IT! and did it DAMN GOOD TO, THANK YOU 2K!. The story is inspired heavily by Heart of Darkness and it's film adaptation Apocalypse Now. It's a lot like watching the chestburster scene in Alien. You can't stand to watch anymore, but you JUST CAN"T LOOK AWAY! After the the first big morals bender (No spoils, but I will say it involves white phosphorose) I actually started to hate myself for my actions. They say that you either die a hero, or live long enouth to see yourself become a villain, and you live very long in this game. psych stuff shows up after a while, just to complete the horror (the horror). make no mystake, it's not a scary horror game, but it is horrifying beyond belief in it's own way.

My only complaints are little nitpics over realism that nobody ever gets right anyway (characters ziplining on their bare fingers, being thrown out of helicopters, falling through floors, and brushing themselves off. nobody ever needs water [even though dehidration becomes a plot-point] etc.) Otherwise, I rate this game 6 out of 5 stars :)

Oh dear... Well i can for starters say that i'm at an disadvantage since i last played the game through about a year ago and i completely forgot that i bought it from Greenman. Also since there is a "credit"-gain from review so.. Might as well.

Before i start, i really should mention that i really cant remember everything about this game. Because of the one year gap. So most of the stuff i say will be mostly about my personal experiences and should be taken with 'nth amount of salt. (Since i'm a little bit biased..)

Well the first thing that needed to be done with the game, was to actually get it to run. Since it had some startup-problems with it, this caused some grey hairs at first, but a quick venture into the promised land of PC-GAMING WIKI. Helped to resolve that problem quickly. Unfortunately, since the game uses encrypted options files. Tweaking other aspects of it will prove difficult, if you wish to, for example, change the FOV.

(I don't remember if the game was updated to include an FOV slider later on.. Again i last played it at the start of 2013.)

Well i think that's the mandatory technical jabber out of the way, onto the game itself.

The story is in itself deceptively straight-forward, it starts of with a group of soldiers, (Delta-Force if memory serves correctly.) On a mission to investigate what happened in Dubai after it was supposed to have been evacuated, before some heavy-duty sandstorms started wrecking up the place.

And that is pretty much the easiest explanation of how the story starts, i really can't write about it that much since i feel i would be doing it no favors. Instead, i will only say that the story only gets more darker and stranger the further it goes. With some actual character-development and i don't mean the "put-points-to-sht-to get-the-biggest-deathcck" -way, but in the storytelling sense. Some of the stuff you see and hear the team say and do really start to show later down the line.

That's enough spoilers for the story part, next!

The gameplay is pretty standart 3rd-person cover-based shooting and that is pretty much the thing that kind of kills the novelty-value almost instantly, because people will automatically make references to any other Military shooter almost instantly. I on the other hand right now started thinking about the Normandy landing scene on Medal of Honor:Allied Assault, nicked almost to the T from Saving private Ryan... Oops Digressing statement.

Later down the line, the game has a turret section, and another, and another yet again.. That kills the feel a bit, since you wonder "Why did it give me another turret section? Can't i just run around and shoot them in the head instead?" Actually, at one point you can, but it makes it a bit harder. But don't get me wrong, the helicopter segment at the start of the game (and the redo of it later) was well executed. I cannot really say the same from the rest though.

Anyway, the biggest sin, i feel from the game-designs part is the linearity. It shows from the start and it carries through to the end. The strangest thing though... I noticed on my last playthrough that i had missed options in the story. All because the game told me to do this, instead of that and now i need to download it again to see the other parts i missed. Since i feel, "if i missed that one so obvious, what others i missed ?"

CONCLUSION:

Even with its story, The Line seems (to untrained eye atleast) a generic 3rd-person shooter. Even the changes the characters go through during the story, kind of brush by with a big red sign over their head saying "FEEL SH_T". And some of the stuff does have some shock value, but it loses even that rather quickly. All and all, the story (if flawed, yes flawed. Shoot me if you disagree.) is the only thing that is interesting about this game. Is it enough to carry it? No. Is it enough to make it stand out from the rest? Yes. Is it actually worth playing? Maybe.

Spec-Ops: The Line is a squad-based third-person shooter, but really this is just a cover-up. The game is actually an experimental arthouse game that tries to challenge conventions of the modern game industry, narrative, and ask the player what they really want from games.

Spec Ops: The Line is the 11th game in the Spec-Ops series, but you'd be forgiven for not knowing that, as the series wasn't particularly great and hadn't had a new entry in its series in over 10 years before this game came along. However, Spec-Ops: The Line is more of a stand-alone game, and you need no knowledge of the previous Spec-Ops games to enjoy it.

You play as Captain Martin Walker, who comes into the town of Dubai under fictional settings that its been ravaged and left for dead by rampant sand storms and riots in the town. A US team, known as the 33rd, was sent there to help keep things under control. The last the city and the 33rd team were recorded doing was trying to form a caravan to help save the survivors of the city. However, all contact was lost, and the city was declared a no-mans land, with access to the city barred off by the UAE government.

Our main character, Walker, comes in with a small team, with the only other members being Lieutenant Alphonse Adams and Staff Sergeant John Lugo. Walker has a personal stake in all of this... The leader of the 33rd, Colonel John Konrad, is a personal hero of his, someone who saved his life on the battlefield. This man changed Walker's life, and is the sort of man Walker inspires to be. So when a communication message from Lugo gets out, he takes on the mission very personally, and is determined to do whatever it takes to save him.

Spec-Ops: The Line is a very beautiful game. Countless scenes and imagery are backed by fantastic artistic design, and one sometimes can't help but to just sit-back and appreciate the aesthetics of it all. The characters are well animated, the effects of things like sand and water are impressive, there are some gorgeous overlooks of the city at various points in the game, and visually stimulating environments that range from theaters to malls to aquariums to the natural desert itself.

The soundtrack is also very stimulating. The game features a variety of licensed music, ranging from Hush by Deep Purple to Star Spangled Banner by Jimi Hendrix. The original soundtrack is also rather interesting, featuring rather ethereal sounds, industrial, and pseudo-rock to home in the tones of each scene. The voicing is handled fantastically, and fits each character rather perfectly.

But there is something looming over Spec-Ops: The Line almost the entire time that may turn off a lot of people. The game isn't really all that fun to play. It's serviceable and not badly made, but something about it makes the gameplay never really a fun experience. And as odd as it may sound, I think this is what the developers were going for. There comes a tedium to the combat, a sort of unfeeling to it all. It can be a struggle at times, and there are some moments that are really cool from a visual stand-point and conceptually so, but it still somehow remains unfun.

Also as someone who played the whole game on hard difficulty, I recommend you do not. I usually play games on the hardest difficulty available as I find it fun to be challenged, but in the case of Spec-Ops I'd argue it actually actively worked to try and make me enjoy the game less. I wasn't having fun with the harder challenges, it didn't feel satisfying to overcome difficult segments, and it caused me to repeat several segments over-and-over again, and not in a way that it was enjoyable.

But I'd still say Spec-Ops is worth experiencing. While the game poses as a third-person shooter, and there is definitely third-person shooter gameplay here, that isn't at the same time really what the game is or is about. Talking about Spec-Ops is difficult, as I believe it is best to go into it without knowing almost anything at all. But at the same time, there is a tedium, a drudgery to pull through in the game.And that arguably is part of the game, and is part of the point of the game and its themes. Spec-Ops has a lot of thought put into it, and is a case where the narrative, atmosphere, and overall experience is much stronger than the gameplay.

Here's an odd analogy; This game is essentially to Shooters what Silent Hill is to Survival-Horror or Braid is to platformers. The games are well-made, but gameplay isn't the focus. Other elements take the lead, and the games have rather strong emphasis on its other elements. The gameplay without these other elements is arguably rather lackluster, or kind of tedious. But with the other elements, the games rise from this to become a rather interesting experience in game form. Some may never see the enjoyment of a game that isn't fun to play from a gameplay perspective, but if you can, there is a lot to love in Spec-Ops: The Line.

It's depressing, sometimes hard to swallow, and you may not honestly understand everything the first time you play it. However, it is likely to stick with you, and really delves into a sort of symbolic social message on shooters and war, and how the general public see's it. It's not very fun, but Spec-Ops is still an experience worth undertaking.

It's a horrible, sickening story, but in the most amazing ways.  It is deeper and far more intelligent than any shooter game I have played.  The controls are not as solid as Gears of War or CoD, but it is worth it in the experience that it provides.  Highly recommended by anyone, especially FPS fans.  Fair warning, nothing you've seen in the CoD franchise is nearly as morbid and heart wrenching.

How can I put this... Spec Ops: The Line is probably one of those games I will remember for a long long time, undoubtedly it's got its ups and downs but overall I, personally, found it masterfully crafter. It however does have some serious drawbacks which dependent upon your gaming style may cause issues.

Pros:
Graphics are pretty masterful, amazing views of Dubai from an unreal perspective
Amazing masterfully crafter storyline which you will most likely not see coming
Pretty great soundtrack with pieces like Glasgow Mega Snakes by Mogwai, and Hush by Deep Purple
Good use of 'sandy' physics, if a little static instead of dynamic. (Basically sand is your friend and your enemy)
Good variety of guns and procedure of getting new better ones.
The game if above easy (Walk on the beach) makes you conserve Ammo
There is amultiplayer/coop gameplay

Cons:
Gameplay needs tightening up.
AI is usually pretty terrible, no matter what difficulty.
Physics are about as static as Call of Duty: Ghosts  (The same bus will always fall at the same point in time after you do the same thing)
Not enough enemy variance.
Multiplayer is very limited.
Co-op is boring and mostly tedious gameplay that isn't properly worked out.

I might add, just for the sake of information, the storyline, from a gamers perspective, is a huge slap in the face, this game will make you regret every choice, no matter of moral superiority, and at the end, well, theres a revelation which will probably change the way you look at games. The way you understand yourself, and there is something to be said of phsychoanalysise, for it is easy to tell what sort of person you are if you are being watched while playing this game. 

This game is more about the gamers than the game itself, at least from my perspective, which makes it doubly interesting.

Anyways in conclusion I love it, I embrace its faults as I do my own and I enjoy its successes which I double do my own. It is a game which must be played once if not anymore and perhaps always looked at to remember what choices you made under pressure, under stress, and if only to shoot people to a song played in the 60's.

Probably not worth it if you are looking for challenging gameplay.

When I first caught a glimpse of this game, I was not intrigued. Sure, the setting seemed original, but I was under the impression that the protagonist/s would be all "hooaah" US soldiers and they were there to fight the local populace. Which, in essence, is a massively overplayed and saturated narrative. Once I played the game, I realised that I made a mistake. I doubt I was ever THIS wrong in my overall assessment of a game before. 

The story line, albeit heavily influenced by the last (or pre-last?) century novel "The Heart of Darkness", manages to remain fresh and relevant, at least in terms of modern military conflicts. I have not been this satisfied by a shooter narrative since Half Life 2. The writing is simply excellent, furiously paced, with twists coming left and right. The voice acting? Phenomenal. The whole cast is a sight to behold (or to hear), but...Nolan North..If I ever were to give out an Oscar for voicing a game character, this would be the case. Cpt. Walkers transformation is simply breath-taking. Sure, in other games, the break-down of a character is often portrayed visually, i.e. blood, torn clothing, injuries..But here, its mainly mental, in the voice. The first time you will hear Walker bellow "Kill is f*cking confirmed", you will know exactly what I mean. 11/10 and then some. 

Visually, its rather a mixed bag. But by no means a BAD mixed bag. Vistas and environments are engaging and beautiful, no qualms there. But maybe sharper/more detailed textures or effects would have been the proverbial icing on the cake for maximum immersion. Either way, you will not be dissapointed, it IS a pretty game. 

Soundtrack wise, this game is a gem. The guitar riffs, as well as the licenced songs from the Vietnam era and what not fit the story and setting like a glove. Small spoiler: When I first encountered the enemy in a certain level, and the accompanying song was "Hush", I knew right there that this game clearly knows how to hit my good buttons :). This is an A-class soundtrack in my book. 

The controls (keyboard) are quite clunky, i.e. on the harder difficulties you will be furious at some points :). It is clear that the game, at least control wise, was mostly intented for consoles. This would probably be the main problem within the game, at least in my opinion.

So would I recommend this game to you? Absolutely. This is truly a breath of fresh air in the TPS/war shooter genre. The creators have shown the game industry that new, fresh and uncompromising ideas DO have a place in todays oversaturated, generic shooter market, and CAN make a difference. I only wish that more games such as this are released more frequently.

TL:DR Version: It's a good solid game with a 4th wall breaking meta narrative on the nature of shooters that ultimately hurts both its story and intended point, but is still something worth experiencing.

Originally when this game came out, it's marketing convinced me that it was another shooter where you killed the "evil Muslims". That they were just arrogant for building that city in the middle of the desert and so on, that I entirely skipped the game and looked on it with scorn. Spec Ops games previously have never given me much reason to think otherwise.

Yet a friend gave me a free copy of the game and I was pretty starved for a good shooter so I gave it a go and what I played ultimately surprised me as much as it confused me, but more on that second part later.

Spec Ops combat is run of the mill on paper. You have guns, you have enemies, you have cover, and you have regenerating health. What sets the game apart is how well it executes each of feature. To say the guns handle well is an over simplification, each of the guns fulfills a unique niche and feel and you quickly develop favorites, followed by attachments to those favorites.

Enemies come sporting some of the better AI I've experienced in shooters along with fluid motion and a sense of self preservation that games like Call of Duty simply lack. They are what make ducking into cover fun. Cover shooting mechanics won't surprise you, but they are as solid as the rest of the game.

My only real complaint about the game is how it trips itself with its own meta narrative on shooters themselves instead of military misadventures or the idea of being a hero. This leads to a lot of confusion at the end of the game that is entirely intentional on the part of the developers. Spec Ops the Line's entire story is literally left up for the player to decide what exactly really happened.

While this is an experience that is worth experiencing it also leaves a profound sense of confusion and a lot of questions that the game could have avoided by not breaking the 4th wall as subtly as it did and went with a more down to earth commentary. It's rather sad, as the game's natural story arch with all its horrific events would have sufficed as a means of getting their point across, but that point becomes rather lost in the confusion and is only discoverable by going online and reading an interview.

Still the game is solid, even if the story harms it a bit from a game standpoint, so I recommend this game, but only to those who can deal with the meta nature of the game. COD fans, you will probably not like this game.

Spec Ops: The Line is a third-person shooter telling the story of US captain Walker, who is sent to Dubai to investigate the failed evacuation of the city after it has been hit by several huge sandstorms.

Gameplay-wise, Spec Ops is your average tps: you need to master taking cover in order to survive and use the game's environment to your advantage (explosives, sand drops, ...). Althought the enemies are kind of repetitive and the various encounters basically the same, the title is entertaining and playable enough. It also spots an average lenght (five or six hours, on an average).

The strongest suits of Spec Ops: The Line are its visuals and atmosphere. The plot and the situations you will find yourself in are basically severe deconstruction on the most abused cliches of modern military shooters. The sanity slippage suffered by the protagonist and the general lack of choices in some instances just add to general surreal theme of the title.

All in all, Spec Ops: The Line is a very atmospheric game and a good gaming experiment in its own right

Spec Ops surprised me. It also shocked me. Not because it is a bad game. In fact it is an amazing game. The reason Spec Ops surprised me and shocked me was because of its story. In the first hour or so you will be thinking "This is a game that is trying to be Call of Duty", which it does but for good reason. It takes the FPS and 3rd Person Military shooters we know and, in a few hours after the game starts, questions you why you like those games so much. Questions like "Why do you like raining fire down upon you enemies" and "Are you sure you want to be a hero?” These questions the game then goes on to answer for you. Without spoiling anything, at the end of the game I loved and hated the game. It gets you thinking "What happened?". Then you play it again to try and understand and start noticing subtle hints.

As for Gameplay mechanics, it is quite like your Gears of War type games, with the cover system and shooting mechanics. You AI buddies help and awful lot and are pretty smart. The terrain can sometimes be used again your opponents and you have a few different selections of guns to choose from, each feeling different. The voice acting is spot on and you will recognise the main characters voice immediately.

This is easily the best game I've ever played. You shouldn't go into this game for gameplay, it isn't anything new but it works perfectly fine with guns being relatively fun to use and enemies having good AI. At times you will find yourself dying a little too quick while some enemies feel like bullet sponges, but that's about right considering how little you wear while they are fully armoured. Now that we're done with the gameplay, the story is the real hook to buying this game. You will find yourself in a gripping story where you are put though many different situations to test your morality, most of which are no win scenarios and give no obvious good choices making you feel worse the more you play. The game is not black and white but rather the complete opposite with the game itself questioning you on whether or not you're really the hero as you fight your way through an entire army in order to find Konrad and end the nightmare he brought to Dubai when him and his soldiers were unable to evacuate this forgotten city. As the game progresses both you and the main protagonist will start to question what's really happening and your current mental state until you reach the ending which left me in such shock that I was left speechless and felt the need to replay the final mission numerous times to see all the endings. I personally felt dead inside after my first run. By the end of my experience I encountered so many twists and turns I didnt know what to expect next and after everything was over, I wanted to go back through the game and make different decisions from my first run to see how my teammates, myself and how everyone around me would react. Overall This was the ultimate video game narrative I've ever experienced and found it more than worth my time, this game took me about 8 hrs to complete due to some moments that took me a few too many tries, keeping it from being fun at all times, but for most people this shouldn't be much longer than 6 hrs though for most who play it on normal difficulty. I found that this game's length was excusable due to the fact that it was so immersive it felt at least twice as long. In the end this game has the best narrative in just about any game I have played so far including Telltale's Walking Dead games and it conveys a great message for the players, making this more than worth the cost.

The mechanics of this game are just horrible and during my whole playthrough I was fighting with myself to turn it off. The only reason I didn't turn the game off is because I've often been told how great the story is, sadly, it's not.

The story does a lot to try and make you feel like a horrible monster and uses some tricks to aid this - sadly, one of the tricks was to give you no choice in some of the deeds you partake in. The second you remove that choice from the player is the second the story disconnects from the player. I'M not the monster, the main character in the game who made those choices is the monster. You are merely the puppetmaster who had to pull the strings for him to do so.

I liked this game alot. 

It's "2DEEP" at times, and tries pretty hard to make you feel like a terrible person for playing it. There's a big argument over the game, mainly that "you could've quit playing at any time!" but ultimately, there's alot of choices that you can't do anything about. The White Phospherous sequence comes to mind. As well as the inability to listen to your orders to not go into the city. 

But then there's scenes where you do get a choice, and if you make the wrong one, you will feel like a terrible human being. There's a sequence where you need to disperse a crowd of civilians. Most people will just open fire and slaughter them, but you can fire into the air to get them to leave peacefully. 

Stuff like that really makes this game have a unique feel to it. The small touches and attention to detail are fantastic, and really support the game's storyline. The protagonist, Walker, is very much not a hero, as you'll come to find out.

The gameplay works, it's nothing special for a cover based TPS game. It does what it needs to do as a vehicle for the story. 

The multiplayer is tacked on, and the devs themselves didn't want to even have a multi-player aspect in the game. The end result is a forced, muddy mess of a game. I would look elsewhere for multiplayer action. 

It's not as clever as alot of people make it out to be, but it's a very self-aware and meta game  none the less. 

It's basically what Ken Levine was trying to go for with Bioshock infinite, except the writing here isn't complete ♥♥♥♥.

First off, BUY AND PLAY THIS GAME!, It's absolutley fantastic!

Secondly, here's why: 

   The story is simply too original to describe, People may overlook this game as a basic mil-spec shooter, but it is NOT! The main focus here is the EFFECTS of war on the soldiers not the shooting, although the mechanics work great and the gameplay feels solid too. The story follows 3 soldiers stranded in a dying Dubai, a Dubai they thought they were there to save. Surrounded by a raging sandstorm that is too strong to break through they fight their way through hostile sand covered streets and buildings to reach their goal of saving the civilians trapped there. Although nothing is what it seems.

The twists and turns the story takes almost put the writing of games like Bioshock and GTA to shame.

GamesRadar.com reviewed the game in their "The best videogame stories ever" article and I feel a direct quote would be sufficient:

"Military shooters don't often rank high on the narrative front, usually favoring gung-ho G.I. Joe antics and flag waving over character development. And, at first, Spec Ops: The Line falls right in line with that stereotype--you take control of Walker, a soldier sent into a sandstorm-ruined Dubai to find a missing general. But as time goes on it becomes more and more obvious that there's something more devious afoot, and the shooter's story transforms from run-of-the-mill to one-of-a-kind.

What unfolds is a damning criticism of shooters themselves, questioning everything that gamers have grown accustom to. Walker's journey sends him marching into the nucleus of the genre, playing with the storytelling in ways no other game has. By the end you might feel anger or sadness, but the important thing is that you'll feel something, and that's pretty rare in military shooters."

I truly feel anyone who can play a shooter, even poorly, NEEDS to experience this game!

Side note, I know it reads out I only have 2.5 hours, but most of the time spent playing through the SP was offline while my internet was disconnected lol.

Let's just say that a certain group of people would have still been alive, if I had known I could have spared their lives without murdering them in cold blood. 

Of course, it is a welcome (and creepy) change of pace when the game starts addressing some messages to you, the player or "special guest", during the loading screens toward the end about some of the moral choices you made earlier in the game ("The Army does not condone the killing of unarmed civilians, but it's only a game, why should you care?")

A somber storyline with actually difficult enemy firefights (i.e. heavies), not to mention endings that made me feel like I completed the game rather than act as a setup for a sequel. makes this game worthwhile to rise to the top among other FPS of this time. Game reminds me a LOT of Binary Domain; another third-person shooter (wall humping and military lingo included) with average gameplay and a fantastic plot. I'm not gonna dwell too long on the game mechanics. It's typical stuff with nothing impressive or worth mentioning. This is one of those games that's more about everything BESIDES the gameplay, which says more about the writing than anything negative about the gameplay. I will only complain about one thing: the game has mechanics that are severely underused. Specifically, silencers, which would let you sneak around getting kills if the game dedicated more to that aspect.

Anyway, the plot is fantastic, and its SPECTACULAR how it handles good and evil. Ultimately, the paradigm (big word alert) is meaningless here; everyone has their motives and reasons for doing what they do. The game weaves a complex narrative that ultimately pins you as neither a 'good guy' nor a 'bad guy'; you are merely someone doing what he believes is right. Emphasis on ''believes'' because all supposedly moral actions in this game are subject to questioning. 

I love the title for that alone. I love when villains are given motives and reasons for their actions other than ''I am bad raawr come get me in my evil evil castle''. They took it a step further by making the protagonist's morality ambiguous as well, and you get to shape some of it along the way. There are some segments where you have to make choices, and the writing makes it so that each option in these segments is a valid choice. Moral choices in games tend to boil down to ''kill grandma; don't kill grandma'', so there's never really any critical thinking involved; developers take note, this game does it right.

I could go on and on about how the pacing is done very well and how I love the narrative. But I'll end on a few unrelated notes:

-For a console game this ♥♥♥♥ looks great. This dude's bald head is so...so [i]bald[/i]. 
-The menu changes as you play the title, which is a cool touch. It's little things like that that give a title some flavor.
-The game is loosely based on an old novel from the 19th century. So, like Binary Domain, it isn't exactly original.
-You might not get sound in pre-rendered cut-scenes. It's a bug having to do with NVIDIA cards or some ♥♥♥♥. Anyway, the fix is insanely simple and there's a thread on the forums about it. Or you could watch pre-rendered stuff on youtube.

The game's pretty short and straight-forward. I love strong narratives so I can't recommend this enough. And while you're at it, pick up Binary Domain as well.

Spec Ops: The Line is, on the surface, a pretty standard third person modern warfare shooter. The most apt comparison in terms of gameplay is probably Call of Duty, but to compare the two is unfair on Spec Ops. In Spec Ops, you have action, violence and smack-talking American soldiers, as you'd expect of any modern shooter. What you probably won't expect is the superb narrative about the morality of war and the toll it takes on the human mind. The setting of Dubai turns out to be the perfect vehicle for this kind of story and the beauty of the landscape contrasts poignantly with the grittiness of the combat.  The soundtrack is also excellent. Clearing out a building of troops to Martha and the Vandellas? Sounds weird, but it's perfect. There are some negatives. The controls are clunky. The cover system is a little restrictive and sticky. The hardest difficulty is frustratingly brutal. Nevertheless, Spec Ops is a gem of a game which gets the combination of action and story just right.

Spec-Ops: The Line is one of those games I remember seeing ads for and thinking "Man, this game looks amazing. I can't wait to play it!" Sadly, it turns out I could. What is supposed to be a "brilliant" deconstruction of the modern FPS genre (never mind this is a third person shooter) instead comes off as yet another half-baked political opinion piece. 

War is Hell, Spec Ops teaches us. Well no ♥♥♥♥; I think we know that, and I think we'd know that even if we weren't given control of the biggest idiot in video game history and forced to commit war crime after war crime for no other reason other than the developer really wants to ram their point home. It'd be one thing if the game were a sort of social experiment, and while it was fully possible to commit atrocities, there were other ways programmed in for the clever, patient, or not braindead player, but sadly this game is yet another linear sewage tunnel with delusions of grandeur. 

While some aspects of the game definately work well (such as being able to slide-kick and tackle enemies from cover), other mechanics (such as any time it becomes necessary to fire a weapon, the cover system itself, and the generic CoD health system) are extremely bland. The combat itself is probably the game's biggest letdown. Aside from the third-person controls, it plays just like every other action game on the market in the last five years: you can carry two weapons at a time, aim down the sights to be more accurate, melee enemies when they get too close, regenerate health just by standing still and willing yourself to heal, etc. The game tries a few things out, such as the squad command mechanics, but these never worked except where they were scripted to do so and even then were even more trouble than they were worth. The environmental mechanics were another touted feature, but again, the ability to bury your enemies alive in several hundred pounds of sand is an option only present at certain plot-centric points and more often than not it's easier just to shoot your way out. Other things that aren't really necessary include several instances (including one entire level) where the player must hang onto something with one hand while defending themsevles with the other. This already looks stupid, and when my character can somehow accurately aim, fire, and RELOAD a Milkor MGL with one hand while hanging off the back of a moving water truck, I have to say the game has jumped the shark. 

The enemies themselves aren't much better: we have a generic rifleman, a generic knife wielder, and the Juggernaut from the Modern Warfare games. Yes, this is definately a new experience.

Overall, Spec Ops: The Line is yet another white-noise entry in the genre, one which will quickly and mercifully fade into oblivion in a few years time.

Spec Ops: The Line is, and at the same time, isnt like every modern military shooter.  It is a Third Person Shooting game set in Dubai with fictional locations. However, the main point of the game isn't to make war out to be some sort of way to make the player out to be a gung-ho badass. It shows a little more of the real side of war, where you see the victims who never wanted any part of it.

There is a multiplayer side to the game, but it feels very tacked on and not worth playing.

If you can find this game for $5 on a Steam sale, or for less anywhere else, definitly pick it up.

They have to investigate on an entire US batallion that vanished during the evacuation operations in the city. Desperately trying to accomplish his mission, the captain begins a descent into darkness and madness. 

Spec ops: the line is an important piece of videogame narration that is entirely based on the topic of moral responsibility. The player has to confront with extreme situations of war and to elaborate on the consequences of his own actions. To me, this is a great strenght of this product, overcoming other lacks in the general gameplay. 

As a tps, there is not so much variety, but at least the battle environments are challenging and appreciable. Someone criticized the game because of bugs and malfunctions. I didn't find them.

The game surprised me with its story and depth.
On the surface it is just another cover-shooter - nothing you have not seen before. But the story and premise is something else, and quite worth your time. Consider it more a cinmetaic experience that you are playing through. The story is well integrated in the actual gameplay, and cut-scenes are not invasive. You'll also find intelligence along the way, that further deepens the story. The voice acting is very well done.

It is very impressive graphically though, and many scenes are beautiful. Detailed face-expressions help the game make it emmotionally immersive.
You are often faced with tough choices that you don't want to make. In the end it does not seem what choice you make, but it still leaves a heavy impact on you.

The combat and mechanics are still good. Guns behave and sound well. The cover mechanics are ok. Sometimes you don't end up doing what you intended to do, but it workds most of the time. Your companions and AI chatters a lot, giving you good intel on the battle field, also further immerse you in the tone and feel of the game.
I like that the enemy has been given a voice and humanity too - you won't always want to attack them.

It seems to be designed with a controller in mind, and it works ok, but mouse and keyboard is still the better experience.

This game is about the story - and does not seem to have any replayability. Mechanics are good, but nothing new. Multiplayer is not really interesting, but the main game was a good experience that kept me hooked through the whole campaign.

Reckommended.

The 3rd person shooter gameplay from minute to minute is solid if a touch clunky at times, but mostly works well. Firefights are satisfactory on the whole with a good balance between player power and AI challange. Enemies appear to move, shoot and behave intelligently on the whole, occasionally flushing you from cover with a well aimed grenade! Cover is plentifal however, and generally affords good protection. The levels are fairly linear but usually there are several routes available in a confrontation, allowing you to flank the enemy and gain the advantage while your teammates provide covering fire.

Where the game really surprises is in the story. What appears at first to be very standard disenguage-brain fodder, quickly heads in a darker and more surprising direction. It complements the atmospheric visuals well and lends a menacing overtone to the whole environment. Suffice it to say it is one of the few game stories where I really wanted to find the outcome, and then to replay to find all the alternative endings.

Overall this is a real surprise. A solid 3rd person military shooter with a dark and enguaging story that will hook you in and drive you through the campaign.

This game.....it will break your sanity. The ending I got was crazy. If it's all based on the choices I made I made some pretty bad ones that I thought were good at the time.

This is a game that needs to be played by anyone who wants to make the argument for games as art. This is one of the best examples of conveying a message directly through player interaction I have seen in a long time.

there is a saying that goes along the lines that what makes art what it is is that it elicits an emotional response from the viewer that is unique to them. This game meets that criteria by all accounts. This is a very emotional game that will test your limits and push you to do actions that will be very difficult to carry out... and I loved every second of it. This is a mature game that handles it's mature theme with the up most respect. you will leave this game with a new appreciation for the medium of video games and it will open your eyes to the impact violence has in video games. It does not tell you that game violence is bad, brainwashing or dangerous. and it also does not tell you that game violence is innocent, harmless or "its just a game". this game allows you to come up with your own judgment and it will open you eyes, regardless of where you stand on the argument and have one hell of a time.

If the phrase, "There is no such thing as a painless lesson." was ever relevent to modern-day media, than Spec-Ops: The Line might as well have it plastered across it's Steam Page like the full-frontal, colossal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that this game is. Seriously, if you've ever been tired of modern military shooters, or just want to be a less horrible person, I fully recommend this game for the story alone. Mechanically, it's pretty run-of-the-mill, combat can get tedious, and your friendly AI is frustrating to work with at times, but it's attention to detail in the enviornments, characters, and atmosphere drive the plot so well that this is one of the most engrossing game narratives that I've ever played. Subject matter is definitely not for the faint of heart, though that is pretty much the point as you're forced to really take a step back and examine the type of standards and themes that other shooters take seemingly for granted.

With a superb story, great soundtrack, and multiple difficulties Spec Ops The Line is easily one of the best third person cover shooters around. Although the story is great, the game play is even better. It says a lot when a game can get you to play through it multiple times on different difficulties just for the challenge of it. While my original experience was a spectacle of story and gameplay the subsequent playthroughs were heightened by the sheer level of enemy difficulty. The increased difficulty changes play a lot. You have to start eliminating targets from afar; and setting yourself up with plenty grenades, quality guns, and ammo before the next checkpoint becomes a must. There are no incredibly lofty achievements tied to this game besides "MFWIC" which requires you complete the game on the dreaded FUBAR difficulty. That experience was as frustrating as it was rewarding. It should also be noted that there are no achievements linked to multiplayer in this game. This is a wonderful game with some less common plot themes.

Not a bad little number. It kept me fairly interested, was a fairly interesting story line all getting tied up in a tight little bow at the end.

It did leave me hanging in the feels department at the end, like i was expecting a little more closure, but i do think thats part of the story its trying to tell.

Good controls, nice visuals, if you've got a good afternoon and evening to blow you could get through the whole thing, but with the way its made, im happy with the purchase.

Spec Ops: The Line...

[i]Ladies and gentlemen... Welcome to Dubai.[/i]


[h1]Story[/h1]

Starting my review with commenting on how good of a story this game had (IMO).
Dramatic twists of events. Taking choices you wouldn't want to. Going through a deep slow path of insanity by each chapter.

I'm usually not amused by any type of story an army game has to offer and I must admit in my eyes most of them are more or less the same.
However out of the bucket of clichés and reused material Spec Ops: The Line stands out.
The fictional concept told here is so well blended that it kept my interest through the whole time from start to end.
I even did 4 runs of the game itself in order to experience all 4 different endings.
Can't say it is original, after the amount of movies and games that have been out so far, there's hardly anything new to be served in militaristic games. However it is the way the content is served that makes the difference in this type of games, this one right here gets the cookie for me.


[h1]Direction[/h1]

The game is very very well directed. The way the story is balanced through action sessions, intense cutscenes, sweet environmental designs, and impressive musical options.
All combined so smoothly with some of the very best voice acting I've seen for an action shooter.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]

Neatly scripted on Unreal Engine 3, the game has sweet physics and sandstorm and smoke dynamics. Of course there have been titles a lot more famous for their graphics for 2012.
But for the experience offered, Spec Ops: The Line's graphics are just perfect and it's lacking major bugs or issues.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

Very easy and comfortable to handle. Ammo and amount of weapons is just about right.
Destructible environment (just a few details here and there) add a good taste on the style of the shooter experience and of course not missing the ability to take cover and using commands to make your crew help you dynamically in various situations.
Difficulty makes a difference from the easiest to the hardest mode and it gets more and more challenging, sometimes kinda too hard in the hardest difficulty level.

[h1]Music[/h1]

The music used in the game is AMAZING.
Not only the acoustic backrgound is very good, but you will also hear a brilliant collection of songs through the game, every single one very accurately put in each situation like a glove.

[h1]Sound[/h1]

Cool environmental and battle effects that seem about right at any moment of the game. No problems with blending music or voice acting.


[h1]Average[/h1]

Considering that this game was implemented by a very small team and the studio itself is not even famous for having any other major titles around the market (Yager Development only have one other game implemented which is very old)
It was freaking amazing. With a story that has a beginning, a peak, and an end. 
Well made, balanced, satisfying, with good action and even a well done multiplayer and co-op modes.
Considering how shallow other a lot more famous games from bigger studios have ended up being, Spec Ops: The Line is by the full meaning of the phrase 'a job well done'.
And for the asked price, this title is pure gold!
Do get it. 100% recommended!

Spec Ops: The Line is a game about morality and introspection. An action/adventure title which grips you with just above average game-play mechanics. Along side that, there is profound situational scenarios that forces an analytical and emotional side from you, with every decision. It may seem like you start as, just, another soldier given, just, another mission. Although, as you act in what seems to be an orderly manner, you begin to question the authenticity, or integrity of such orders. You begin to question because of the veracious nature of these orders. It becomes difficult and even, regretful, when you persist to just 'follow orders.' 

It is a game which for the most part of the story, is confusing. Your distaste by all the violence you do as this character, I don't want to give any spoilers but there are some really deep philosophical questions that the game provokes from you, after these unfortunate situations. All that thought, accumulates into a severe confusion and doubt about where this is all going. Why so much pain? So much death?...Well, the ending holds a powerful question, the question is what will you do?

In regards to the game-play mechanics, they're inherently superficial and refined. This allows for the player to not completely focus on just the action, but the scenery, the sounds, the presentation of a doomed Dubai. There were many breathtaking scenes, in which I have numerous images for.

There is only one reason one should purchase this game, it is if you are looking for a intellectually provocative game. Take head tho, there is alot of filler action. Seemingly useless scenes of violence. Furthermore, I would like to add, that discussing such an issue, as this game does, with such a small script, was impressive. I hope the studio is working on the next of the series, maybe one that jumps further deep into the monstrous acts of war, and the repercussions of those wars.

[u][b]Spec Ops: The Line[/b][/u]

The Line is at once one of the best military games I have ever played and one of the darkest experiences I've encountered. Definitely worth playing through at least once through the entire game, and repeat the last 2 levels to experience all 4 endings.

[b][u]Pros[/u][/b]
- Mature, engaging storyline, one of the few around. 
- Solid shooting mechanics.
- Solid, if light, squad mechanics. 
- Variety, especially in set pieces.
- Challenging, 'just right' difficulty (on normal).

[b][u]Cons[/u][/b]
- With the exception of the very detailed character models, graphics are mostly plain and serviceable.
- Squad AI can occasionally be a bit wonky.
- Only ran accross a couple of bugs, but both were gamebreakers and required a checkpoint reload.
- Short game. Over in roughly 5 hours, a solid gamer on easy could probably clear through this in 4.

[b][u]Verdict[/u][/b]
Definitely worth playing through for the storyline. It takes a bit to get going ([spoiler]the 'hook' is on level 6[/spoiler]), but it doesn't tire the gamer. I doubt I'd pay full price for 5 hours worth of entairtainment, even of this caliber, but if you can find it in a sale, definitely check it out.

The Dubai Game! Really, just for its setting it's worth being played. Spec Ops puts you in the shoes of a Delta Force squad leader who - along with two members of the same squad - must uncover the truth behind the disappearance of a famous colonel. Search is immediately started after receiving a radio signal and your squad eventually finds itself in the middle of a war.

The game is a relatively difficult tactical 3rd person shooter - you control the leader but can give orders to the squad members.  You clear one room after the next - while the game is linear it offers a great story that tries to portray the dark side of a war, a war where it's almost impossible to make good choices. The game has stunning visuals and superb voice acting - all delivered from the best in the gaming industry. Replayability exists due to the different difficulties and also the different endings offered based on the choices to be made by the players.

I never tried its multiplayer mode but did not plan to do so. Just for the single player experience this is a highly recommended game not just for those in favour of the genre but for those who like a good story.

I am very surprised to see the low score on metacritic.  I am admittedly not a hardcore shooter fan, but this game is great.  This isn't a "good guys vs bad guys" game, or a pointless shoot'em'up with cutscenes.  This is a game that does its best to suck the player in and make them feel the gravity of a hopeless situation.  It is designed to make you feel that combat is hellish and man some of the scenes is this game would be horribly haunting if they ever happen in reality.  You make quick and tough decisions and sometimes there really doesn't seem like a right answer.  I love the dark storyline and the controls are no worse than any other game I have ever played... I highly recommend it to anyone who likes challenging gameplay and a compelling storyline to return to.
